subproblem.title: Basic calculus of integer multiplicity representations: locality of approximate tangent spaces, restriction, differences, orientation bound
subproblem.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M M' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet M → MeasurableSet M' → M ⊆ M' → M' ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (M' ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → ∃ (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents A ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

(c) Differences. Let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, be represented by R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) and R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B).
1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers). Let G be the set of x ∈ M_A ∪ M_B such that: if x ∈ M_A, then ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x) and there is Q_A(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_A x Q_A(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_A x) Q_A(x); the analogous condition for B if x ∈ M_B; and, for each pair (N, N') among (M_A ∩ M_B, M_A), (M_A ∩ M_B, M_B) with x ∈ N, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q for every Q. By the orientation fields of R_A, R_B, by (P6) and by (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ ⊇ (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0).
2. (Overlap.) Let x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀. The approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x exists and equals Q_A(x) and also Q_B(x) (the equivalences defining G and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); so Q_A(x) = Q_B(x) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. Put ε(x) := 1 if ξ̃_B(x) = ξ̃_A(x) and ε(x) := −1 otherwise (a Borel function).
3. (Data.) Put O := (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀, k := θ_A − εθ_B ∈ ℤ on O, and
 M := ((M_A ∖ M_B) ∪ (M_B ∖ M_A) ∪ {x ∈ O : k(x) ≠ 0}) ∖ N₀,
 θ := θ_A on M_A ∖ M_B, θ_B on M_B ∖ M_A, |k| on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued),
 ζ := ξ̃_A on M_A ∖ M_B, −ξ̃_B on M_B ∖ M_A, sign(k)ξ̃_A on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel).
For every x ∉ N₀: θ(x)1_M(x)ζ(x) = θ_A(x)1_{M_A}(x)ξ̃_A(x) − θ_B(x)1_{M_B}(x)ξ̃_B(x) (on O with k = 0 both sides vanish; on O with k ≠ 0, θ_Aξ̃_A − θ_Bεξ̃_A = kξ̃_A = |k| sign(k)ξ̃_A; the other cases are immediate).
4. (Representation.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), integrating ⟨ω, ·⟩ against both sides of step 3 (N₀ is null; all integrands are integrable by (d), since θ1_M ≤ θ_A1_{M_A} + θ_B1_{M_B}):
 ∫_M θ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M_A} θ_A⟨ω, ξ_A⟩ dHⁿ − ∫_{M_B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ = A(ω) − B(ω) = (A − B)(ω).
5. (Structure fields.) M is Borel, M ⊆ M_A ∪ M_B ⊆ U, and M is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_iUnion, CountablyRectifiable.mono). θ is Borel and ℕ-valued with θ ≥ 1 on M (|k| ≥ 1 where k ≠ 0), and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M_A∩K} θ_A dHⁿ + ∫_{M_B∩K} θ_B dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
6. (Orientation.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M_A ∩ K) + Hⁿ(M_B ∩ K) < ∞ by (P6) applied to R_A, R_B. Apply (a) to the pairs (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M_A), (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M_B), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M) (all Borel, contained in U, with locally finite Hⁿ-measure): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M_A the approximate tangent spaces of M and of M_A at x coincide (both equal that of M ∩ M_A), and similarly for M_B. Let x be such a point, x ∉ N₀. If x ∈ M_A, then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_A(x) and ζ(x) = ±ξ_A(x) (cases M_A ∖ M_B and O, using ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x)), a unit orientation of Q_A(x) by (P5). If x ∈ M_B ∖ M_A, ζ(x) = −ξ_B(x) is a unit orientation of Q_B(x), the approximate tangent space of M at x. Hence the orientation field holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M.
So (M, θ, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing A − B, and A − B is integer multiplicity. ∎

Consequences used by siblings. (i) By (c), 0 = B − B, −B = 0 − B and A + B := A − (0 − B) are integer multiplicity whenever A, B are, hence so is every finite integer combination of integer multiplicity currents in an open set. (ii) The zero current is integer multiplicity even when no integer multiplicity current is given: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero; the positivity, integrability, measurability and orientation fields hold vacuously because μHE restricted to ∅ is the zero measure; the representing integral over ∅ is 0). This is a direct check, not part of the Lean statement; siblings repeat it where needed. (iii) By (d), for an IMRep R, (R.measure, R.orient) satisfies the a.e. bound |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| required by the sibling slicing.
Remark (reuse; not a proof step). Comparator-accepted DAG declarations cover parts of this proof: regcomp_approx_tangent_locality (and rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset, same type) is part (a) with A := M, B := M' and the two sides of ↔ exchanged; regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le (|α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for orthonormal τ) is the inequality of (P4), from which (d) follows by the orientation field; rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg is (P5); dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub is part (c) under the extra hypothesis 0 < n (the case n = 0 is still covered by the argument above, which does not use n ≥ 1).
proof_key_steps: (d): Cauchy–Binet gives Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = 1 for orthonormal τ, so |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
(a): the density of Hⁿ⌞(M′∖M) vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6 on an exhaustion of U), so the blow-up integrals of M and M′ have the same limits.
(b): all IMRep fields restrict; the orientation field transfers by (a); continuity of the restricted current from local integrability and (d).
(c): on the overlap the approximate tangent spaces agree a.e., so the orientations differ by a sign; combine multiplicities θ_A ∓ θ_B, drop cancellation points, and verify the IMRep fields with (a).

subproblem.title: Mass on open sets of an integer multiplicity current equals its representation measure (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (contract IMRep U n): M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable; θ : ℝ^P → ℕ Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n spanning an approximate tangent space of M at x with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all α, or ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all α. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be represented by R: T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Put μ_R(A) := ∫_{M∩A} θ dHⁿ (the contract's R.measure). Then for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = μ_R(W), where M_W(T) := sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn) and |α| := (Σ_{1≤i_1<⋯<i_n≤P} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors (Simon 6.1.15, 6.2.5).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768), stated there without proof; the argument is the one indicated in Remark 2.6 (properties (a), (b) of the norm) together with 2.7–2.8 (lines 243–283). Write E for the space of n-covectors on ℝ^P with the inner product ⟨α, α'⟩_E := Σ_I α(e_I) α'(e_I) (sum over increasing n-tuples I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n), e_I := (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})); its norm is |·|. If n > P then E = 0, every n-form vanishes, so T = 0 and M_W(T) = 0, and Hⁿ = 0 on ℝ^P (Hausdorff dimension P < n), so μ_R = 0 and the claim holds. Assume n ≤ P.
1. (Algebra.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let A be the n×P matrix A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩. Expanding each τ_i in the standard basis, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I), where A_I is the n×n submatrix of A with columns I. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2}, and by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E. The covector α_τ(v_1, …, v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} satisfies α_τ(e_I) = det(A_I); hence ⟨α, α_τ⟩_E = α(τ) for every α, |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ) = 1. (For n = 0 everything is trivial: α(τ) = α(∅) and |α| = |α(∅)|.)
2. (Consequences on M.) Let J : E* → E be the Riesz isomorphism (⟨α, J(η)⟩_E = η(α)) and β := J ∘ ξ, an Hⁿ⌞M-measurable E-valued map. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M we have ξ(x) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) with τ orthonormal, so by step 1: |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E, β(x) = ±α_τ, |β(x)| = 1 and ⟨β(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 1.
3. (Integrability.) For every compact K ⊆ U, μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), then tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ (sup|ω|)·θ·1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so the integrand is integrable and T(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R.
4. (Upper bound.) Let ω be admissible: ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1, and ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 0 if x ∉ W. Hence T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W), so max(T(ω), 0) ≤ μ_R(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound: reduction to compact sets.) V := U ∩ W is open and μ_R(W) = μ_R(V) since M ⊆ U. V is the increasing union of the compact sets K_i := {x ∈ V : |x| ≤ i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) ≥ 1/i} (K_i := {|x| ≤ i} if V = ℝ^P), so μ_R(V) = sup_i μ_R(K_i). It therefore suffices to prove M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for every compact K ⊆ V and every η > 0. Fix K and η; if μ_R(K) = 0 there is nothing to prove.
6. (Open neighbourhood.) Choose δ > 0 with {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 2δ} ⊆ V. The sets O_s := {x : dist(x, K) < s}, 0 < s ≤ δ, have compact closures contained in V ⊆ U, so μ_R(O_δ) < ∞ and μ_R(O_s) ↓ μ_R(K) as s ↓ 0 (continuity from above; K is closed). Fix s ∈ (0, δ] with μ_R(O ∖ K) < η, where O := O_s.
7. (Lusin.) μ_R⌞K is a finite Borel measure on a compact metric space and β is μ_R-measurable; by Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01/Lusin.lean) there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that β|K' is continuous; by inner regularity we may also assume that |β| = 1 and ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1 at every point of K' (these hold μ_R-a.e. by step 2).
8. (Continuous extension.) By Tietze's extension theorem (applied to the coordinates of β in a basis of E), β|K' extends to a continuous g_0 : ℝ^P → E. Let r : E → E be the radial retraction r(α) := α if |α| ≤ 1, r(α) := α/|α| otherwise (continuous, |r| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball). By Urysohn's lemma choose a continuous χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on K' and tsupport χ ⊆ O compact. Put g := χ·(r ∘ g_0). Then g is continuous, tsupport g ⊆ O is compact, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere, and g = β on K'.
9. (Smoothing.) Let φ_σ (σ > 0) be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_σ = 1, supported in the closed σ-ball) and g_σ := g * φ_σ (componentwise convolution). Then g_σ is C^∞, tsupport g_σ ⊆ {x : dist(x, tsupport g) ≤ σ} ⊆ O for 0 < σ < dist(tsupport g, ℝ^P ∖ O), |g_σ(x)| ≤ ∫ |g(x − y)| φ_σ(y) dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_σ → g uniformly as σ ↓ 0 (g is uniformly continuous). Viewed as an n-form, g_σ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (compact support in O ⊆ U) and g_σ is admissible for M_W(T) (O ⊆ V ⊆ W, |g_σ| ≤ 1).
10. (Estimate.) By steps 2–3, |T(g_σ) − ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R| ≤ sup|g_σ − g|·μ_R(closure O) → 0 as σ ↓ 0. On K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ = ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1; on O ∖ K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ ≥ −|g| ≥ −1 μ_R-a.e.; off O, g = 0. Hence ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(O ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − η) − (μ_R(O ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K')) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3η. Therefore max(T(g_σ), 0) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for σ small, and M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η.
11. By step 5, M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞); together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W). ∎
Remark (reuse; not a proof step). Step 4 proves M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) and steps 5–11 prove μ_R(W) ≤ M_W(T) for open W. The comparator-accepted DAG declarations dor_ims_massOn_le_measure, of frozen type ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W, and dor_ims_measure_le_massOn, of frozen type ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → R.measure W ≤ T.massOn W, state these two inequalities (the first even without openness of U and W), so a decomposition of this child may reuse them verbatim and conclude by antisymmetry.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: for a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm), with equality for the dual covector β = J∘ξ, |β| = 1.
Upper bound: T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for admissible ω, so M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lower bound: inner regularity reduces to compact K ⊆ U ∩ W; Lusin, Tietze, radial truncation, a cut-off and mollification give smooth admissible forms g_σ with T(g_σ) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η.

subproblem.title: Riesz representation of currents of locally finite mass, and absolute continuity of normal currents (Simon Ch. 6, 2.7–2.8, 2.36–2.37)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) a current (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n) with M_W(T) < ∞ for every open W with closure(W) compact and contained in U. Then there are a Borel measure μ on ℝ^P and a map ξ from ℝ^P to n-vectors (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) such that: μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0; μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P; ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable; |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every x and every n-covector α, where |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm); T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); and, if in addition M_W(∂T) < ∞ for every such W (boundaryMassOn, read as 0 when n = 0), then μ(E) = 0 for every set E ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(E) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → T.massOn W < ∞) → ∃ (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), μ Uᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) ∧ (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = μ W) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ ∧ (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) ∧ ((∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → boundaryMassOn T W < ∞) → ∀ E : Set (Euclid P), μHE[n] E = 0 → μ E = 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.7–2.8 (Riesz representation of currents of locally finite mass, chapter-06.txt lines 265–283), 2.35–2.37 (absolute continuity of normal currents, lines 606–660; printed pages 143–145). Simon proves 2.36 through the BV structure theorem 2.35 (which rests on BV compactness, Ch. 2, 2.6); here 2.35 is replaced by the elementary estimate of step 8 (mollification plus the Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality, which is in Mathlib), and the rest of 2.36 is Simon's projection argument.

Notation. 𝒟ⁿ(U) is the space of test forms in U (TestFormOn U n). For an n-covector α on ℝ^P, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, e_I := (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n}). Let 𝕀 be the finite set of these I and H := EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝕀; the map c(α) := (α(e_I))_{I∈𝕀} is a linear isomorphism onto H — injective because an alternating form is determined by its values on increasing tuples of basis vectors, surjective because the coordinate covectors dx^I(v_1, …, v_n) := det((v_j)^{i_k})_{k,j} (built from Mathlib's determinant of the matrix of coordinates, an alternating multilinear map) satisfy dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} — and |α| = ‖c(α)‖_H; every n-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. If n > P then 𝕀 = ∅ and every n-covector is 0 (any n > P vectors are linearly dependent, and alternating maps vanish on linearly dependent families, Mathlib AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). For a form ω put |ω|_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)|. An n-vector (MultiVector P n) is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors; ⟨α, ζ⟩ := ζ(α).

Elementary facts used below.
(E1) If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W with W open and W ⊂⊂ U, then |T(ω)| ≤ |ω|_∞·M_W(T). Proof: if |ω|_∞ = 0 then ω = 0. Otherwise ±ω/|ω|_∞ are admissible for M_W(T) (massAdmissibleOn), so ±T(ω)/|ω|_∞ ≤ M_W(T).
(E2) For a 1-covector β and a k-covector γ, |β ∧ γ| ≤ |β||γ|; for an orthogonal projection (or any linear map with orthonormal coordinate structure) p_α : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ, x ↦ (x^{i_1}, …, x^{i_n}), and a k-covector γ on ℝⁿ, |p_α^#γ| = |γ|. Proof: k!|γ|² = Σ_{i_1,…,i_k} γ(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_k})² (each increasing tuple occurs k! times up to sign; tuples with repetitions vanish), and the right side is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear form γ, which does not depend on the orthonormal basis; so |·| is invariant under orthogonal changes of coordinates; rotate so that β = |β|e^1; then β∧γ = |β| Σ_{I∌1} γ_I e^1∧e^I and its norm is |β|(Σ_{I∌1}γ_I²)^{1/2} ≤ |β||γ|. For p_α, p_α^# maps the coordinate covector e^J of ℝⁿ (J ⊆ {1..n}) to the coordinate covector e^{α(J)} of ℝ^P, an isometric embedding of the orthonormal bases.
(E3) If ζ is a unit simple n-vector or more generally |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| for all α, then for every form ω, |⟨ω(x), ζ⟩| ≤ |ω(x)|.

Proof.

Part I: representation, properties (1)–(6) of the statement (μ Uᶜ = 0, finiteness on compacts, M_W(T) = μ(W), measurability, |ξ| ≤ 1, T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ).

1. (Trivial case n > P.) Then every n-covector vanishes (Notation), every test form is 0, T = 0, M_W(T) = 0 for all W; μ := 0 and ξ := 0 satisfy all assertions, including the last one. Assume n ≤ P.

2. (Extension to continuous forms.) Let X := U with the subspace topology (open in ℝ^P, hence locally compact, Hausdorff and second countable). For g ∈ C_c(X, H) let g̃ : ℝ^P → (n-covectors) be g̃(x) := c^{-1}(g(x)) for x ∈ U and g̃(x) := 0 otherwise; g̃ is continuous with compact support spt g ⊆ U. Fix a compact set C ⊆ U containing spt g and an open W with C ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U (e.g. W := thickening δ C = {x : ∃ y ∈ C, |x − y| < δ} with 2δ < infDist(C, ℝ^P ∖ U), δ := 1 if U = ℝ^P; W = ∅ if C = ∅, in which case g = 0 and L(g) := 0). Let (φ_σ)_{σ>0} be a standard mollifier on ℝ^P (C^∞, ≥ 0, ∫φ_σ = 1, support in the closed σ-ball; Mathlib ContDiffBump.normed). For 0 < σ < dist(C, ℝ^P ∖ W), g_σ := g̃ ∗ φ_σ (componentwise in the coordinates α(e_I)) is C^∞ with tsupport g_σ ⊆ C + B̄_σ ⊆ W, so g_σ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); g_σ → g̃ uniformly as σ ↓ 0 (uniform continuity of g̃); and |g_σ(x)| ≤ ∫|g̃(x − y)|φ_σ(y) dy ≤ |g̃|_∞ (convexity of the norm). By (E1), |T(g_σ) − T(g_τ)| ≤ |g_σ − g_τ|_∞ M_W(T) → 0, so L(g) := lim_{σ↓0} T(g_σ) exists. More generally, if (h_k), (h'_k) are sequences in 𝒟ⁿ(U) with supports in a fixed open W' ⊂⊂ U and h_k, h'_k → g̃ uniformly, then |T(h_k) − T(h'_k)| ≤ |h_k − h'_k|_∞ M_{W'}(T) → 0 (E1); since the union of two open sets compactly contained in U is again compactly contained in U, L(g) does not depend on the mollifier or on C, W. Consequently: (a) L : C_c(X, H) → ℝ is linear; (b) L(ω|_U) = T(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (constant sequence); (c) |L(g)| ≤ |g̃|_∞ M_W(T) = sup‖g‖_H · M_W(T) whenever spt g ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U, W open. In particular L is locally bounded in the sense of SimonGMT IsLocallyBoundedCcFunctional: for compact C ⊆ X choose W ⊂⊂ U open with C ⊆ W; then L(g) ≤ M_W(T) < ∞ whenever ‖g‖ ≤ 1 and spt g ⊆ C.

3. (Riesz representation.) By SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory (X locally compact Hausdorff, H a finite-dimensional, hence separable, real inner product space, L locally bounded) there are the Radon measure μ₀ := vectorFunctionalEnvelopeMeasure L on X (regular, finite on compact sets: vectorFunctionalEnvelopeMeasure_isRadon) and ν : X → H, measurable for the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ₀, with ‖ν‖ = 1 μ₀-a.e. and L(g) = ∫⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩_H dμ₀(x) for all g ∈ C_c(X, H) (the Carathéodory extension agrees with μ₀ on Borel sets). Moreover (simon_theorem_4_14_positive_envelope) for every f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ_{≥0}),
 (3a) sup{L(g) : g ∈ C_c(X, H), ‖g(x)‖ ≤ f(x) ∀x} = ∫ f dμ₀.
Passage to a Borel version: μ₀ is σ-finite (X is σ-compact and μ₀ is finite on compact sets), so every set measurable for the Carathéodory σ-algebra of the outer measure of μ₀ is μ₀-null-measurable, and the Carathéodory measure radonCaratheodoryMeasure μ₀ has the same null sets as μ₀ and agrees with it on Borel sets (SimonGMT Chapter01 radonCaratheodoryMeasure_apply and integral_radonCaratheodoryMeasure). Hence ν agrees μ₀-a.e. with a Borel map ν_B, and L(g) = ∫⟨g, ν_B⟩ dμ₀ for g ∈ C_c(X, H) (the integrand is Borel); redefine ν_B := 0 on the Borel μ₀-null set where ‖ν_B‖ ≠ 1, so ‖ν_B(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x and the representation of L is unchanged.

4. (Definition of μ and ξ.) Let μ be the push-forward of μ₀ under the inclusion U ↪ ℝ^P, a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 and μ(C) = μ₀(C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ U. For x ∈ U let ξ(x) be the n-vector α ↦ ⟨c(α), ν_B(x)⟩_H, and ξ(x) := 0 for x ∉ U. Then ξ is Borel (finite-dimensional target), hence a.e. strongly measurable for μ, and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖c(α)‖‖ν_B(x)‖ ≤ |α| for all x, α (Cauchy–Schwarz). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), step 2(b) and step 3 give T(ω) = L(ω|_U) = ∫_U ⟨c(ω(x)), ν_B(x)⟩ dμ₀ = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x), the integrand being bounded by |ω|_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}, which is μ-integrable.

5. (M_W(T) = μ(W) for open W.) Upper bound: if ω is admissible for M_W(T) (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1) then T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω) dμ ≤ μ(tsupport ω) (a finite real number, since ξ(x)(ω(x)) ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1_{tsupport ω}(x)), so ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ μ(tsupport ω) ≤ μ(W) in [0, ∞]. Hence M_W(T) = sup ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ μ(W). Lower bound: μ(W) = μ₀(W ∩ U) = sup{μ₀(C) : C ⊆ W ∩ U compact} (inner regularity of the Radon measure μ₀ on the open set W ∩ U). Fix such C and ε > 0. Choose f ∈ C_c(X, [0, 1]) with f = 1 on C and spt f ⊆ W ∩ U (Urysohn). By (3a) there is g ∈ C_c(X, H) with ‖g‖ ≤ f and L(g) ≥ ∫ f dμ₀ − ε ≥ μ₀(C) − ε. Mollify as in step 2 with σ < dist(spt f, ℝ^P ∖ (W ∩ U)): g_σ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport g_σ ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_σ| ≤ 1, and T(g_σ) → L(g). So for small σ, g_σ is admissible for M_W(T) and T(g_σ) ≥ μ₀(C) − 2ε. Hence M_W(T) ≥ μ₀(C) − 2ε, and M_W(T) ≥ μ(W). (Both sides may be ∞.)

6. Steps 4 and 5 give all assertions except the last. In particular, for every open G and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω| ≤ 1, T(ω) ≤ μ(G), and the following uniqueness fact holds: (U1) if two finite signed Borel measures κ, κ' on an open set G satisfy ∫ b dκ = ∫ b dκ' for all b ∈ C_c^∞(G), then κ = κ' on Borel subsets of G (for compact C ⊆ G, smooth 0 ≤ b_k ≤ 1 with b_k ↓ 1_C pointwise and supports in a fixed compact subset of G exist; dominated convergence gives κ(C) = κ'(C); compact sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra of G and both are finite).

Part II: absolute continuity (the last assertion). Assume M_W(∂T) < ∞ (boundaryMassOn) for every open W ⊂⊂ U. If n = 0, μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero, hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton), so μHE[0](E) = 0 forces E = ∅ and μ(E) = 0. If n > P, μ = 0 (step 1). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ P.

7. (Reduction.) Let E ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(E) = 0 (Hⁿ := μHE[n]). Hⁿ is Borel regular, so there is a Borel E' ⊇ E with Hⁿ(E') = 0; replacing E by E' ∩ U (μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0) we may assume E is Borel and E ⊆ U. μ is a Borel measure on ℝ^P which is finite on compact subsets of the open set U and vanishes outside U, hence inner regular on Borel sets (it is locally finite on the σ-compact Polish space U); so it suffices to show μ(C) = 0 for every compact C ⊆ U with Hⁿ(C) = 0. Fix such C and an open W with C ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U (as in step 2). Then μ(W) = M_W(T) < ∞ and M_W(∂T) < ∞.

8. (Lemma TD: top-dimensional normal measures are absolutely continuous.) Let 1 ≤ n, let m be a finite signed Borel measure on ℝⁿ with compact support, and suppose
 Λ := sup{|∫ div g dm| : g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ; ℝⁿ), |g(y)| ≤ 1 ∀y} < ∞.
Then |m|(N) = 0 for every Lⁿ-null set N ⊆ ℝⁿ.
Proof. Let u_σ := φ_σ ∗ m, i.e. u_σ(y) := ∫ φ_σ(y − z) dm(z), with φ_σ a mollifier on ℝⁿ; u_σ is C^∞ with compact support (in spt m + B̄_σ) and ∂_j u_σ(y) = ∫ ∂_jφ_σ(y − z) dm(z) (differentiation under the integral, m finite). For g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ; ℝⁿ), Fubini gives ∫ ∇u_σ · g dy = ∫∫ ∇φ_σ(y − z)·g(y) dy dm(z) = −∫ div(φ̌_σ ∗ g) dm with (φ̌_σ ∗ g)(z) := ∫ φ_σ(y − z) g(y) dy, a smooth compactly supported field with |φ̌_σ ∗ g| ≤ 1 when |g| ≤ 1. Hence |∫∇u_σ·g| ≤ Λ for all such g, and since ∇u_σ is continuous with compact support, ∫|∇u_σ| dy ≤ Λ (take g_k := χ_k ∇u_σ/(|∇u_σ|² + 1/k)^{1/2} with smooth cut-offs χ_k ↑ 1, |g_k| ≤ 1, and use monotone convergence). If n ≥ 2, the Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality (Mathlib MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_one, applied on ℝⁿ with p = n/(n−1), the Hölder conjugate of n = finrank ℝⁿ, and ‖fderiv u_σ‖ = |∇u_σ|) gives ‖u_σ‖_{L^{n/(n−1)}} ≤ C_n Λ. If n = 1, u_σ(y) = ∫_{−∞}^y u_σ' so sup|u_σ| ≤ Λ. For a ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ), Fubini gives ∫ u_σ a dy = ∫ (φ̌_σ ∗ a) dm → ∫ a dm as σ ↓ 0 (φ̌_σ ∗ a → a uniformly and |m| is finite). By Hölder, |∫ a dm| ≤ C_n Λ ‖a‖_{L^n} (n ≥ 2), resp. ≤ Λ‖a‖_{L^1} (n = 1). For an open set G, |m|(G) = sup{∫ a dm : a ∈ C_c^∞(G), |a| ≤ 1} (Hahn decomposition and inner regularity of the finite Borel measure |m| on G, approximating 1_{P∩C} − 1_{N∩C} for compact C by smooth functions and dominated convergence), hence |m|(G) ≤ C_nΛ Lⁿ(G)^{1/n}, resp. ≤ Λ L¹(G). If Lⁿ(N) = 0, outer regularity of Lⁿ gives open G ⊇ N with Lⁿ(G) arbitrarily small, so |m|(N) = 0. ∎

9. (Projection argument; Simon 2.36.) For a multi-index α = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) ∈ 𝕀 let p_α : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ, x ↦ (x^{i_1}, …, x^{i_n}), and dx^α := dx^{i_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{i_n}. p_α is 1-Lipschitz, so Hⁿ(p_α(C)) ≤ Hⁿ(C) = 0 (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le), and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (μHE[n] on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is the volume, Mathlib Geometry/Euclidean/Volume); so N_α := p_α(C) is a compact Lⁿ-null set. Let λ_α be the finite signed Borel measure on W given by dλ_α := ⟨dx^α, ξ⟩ dμ⌞W (|⟨dx^α, ξ⟩| ≤ |dx^α| = 1, μ(W) < ∞). For b ∈ C_c^∞(W) let m_{α,b} := (p_α)_*(b λ_α), a finite signed measure on ℝⁿ supported in p_α(spt b) (compact). For g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ; ℝⁿ) put γ := Σ_j g_j ε_j with ε_j := (−1)^{j−1} dy^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dy^{j−1} ∧ dy^{j+1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dy^n (the factor dy^j omitted), so that dγ = (div g) dy and |γ(y)| = |g(y)|. Then p_α^#((div g)dy) = d(p_α^#γ), and by step 4 (applied to the test form b·p_α^#((div g) dy) ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), supported in spt b ⊆ W):
 ∫ div g dm_{α,b} = ∫ b(x)(div g)(p_α x)⟨dx^α, ξ(x)⟩ dμ(x) = T(b·d(p_α^#γ)) = T(d(b p_α^#γ)) − T(db ∧ p_α^#γ) = ∂T(b p_α^#γ) − T(db ∧ p_α^#γ).
By (E1) and (E2) (|p_α^#γ| = |γ| ≤ 1, |db ∧ p_α^#γ| ≤ |db|), the absolute value is ≤ |b|_∞ M_W(∂T) + |db|_∞ M_W(T) < ∞ whenever |g| ≤ 1. By step 8, |m_{α,b}|(N_α) = 0, i.e.
 ∫_{p_α^{-1}(N_α)} b dλ_α = m_{α,b}(N_α) = 0 for every b ∈ C_c^∞(W).
By (U1) applied to the finite signed measures 1_{p_α^{-1}(N_α)}λ_α and 0 on W, λ_α(B ∩ p_α^{-1}(N_α)) = 0 for every Borel B ⊆ W; since C ⊆ p_α^{-1}(N_α), ∫_C h dλ_α = 0 for every bounded Borel h on W.

10. (Conclusion.) Let ω be admissible for M_W(T) and write ω = Σ_{α∈𝕀} ω_α dx^α with ω_α ∈ C_c^∞(W). By step 4 and step 9 (h := ω_α),
 T(ω) = Σ_α ∫ ω_α dλ_α = Σ_α ∫_C ω_α dλ_α + ∫_{W∖C} ξ(ω) dμ = ∫_{W∖C} ξ(ω) dμ ≤ μ(W ∖ C).
Taking the supremum, μ(W) = M_W(T) ≤ μ(W ∖ C); since μ(W) < ∞, μ(C) = 0. By step 7, μ(E) = 0 for every E with Hⁿ(E) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Extend T by mollification to a locally bounded linear functional L on C_c(U; Λⁿ) with |L(g)| ≤ sup|g|·M_W(T).
Apply the SimonGMT vector Riesz theorem (simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory) to get μ₀ and a unit field ν; push μ₀ to ℝ^P and set ξ(x)(α) := ⟨c(α), ν(x)⟩.
M_W(T) = μ(W): ≤ from the representation; ≥ from the positive-envelope identity, inner regularity, Urysohn and mollification.
Lemma TD: a compactly supported signed measure on ℝⁿ whose distributional gradient has finite mass is absolutely continuous (mollify, Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev for n ≥ 2, direct bound for n = 1).

Simon 2.36: push T⌞b dx^α forward by the coordinate projections p_α; TD shows these measures do not charge p_α(C) for Hⁿ-null compact C, hence M_W(T) ≤ μ(W ∖ C) and μ(C) = 0; inner regularity finishes.

subproblem.title: Convergence of integrals from limsup on compact sets and liminf on open sets
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and μ, μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) Borel measures on ℝ^P such that (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ U; (c) μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for every open G ⊆ U (lim sup and lim inf in [0, ∞]). Then ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ (Bochner integrals) for every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → limsup (fun j => μs j K) atTop ≤ μ K) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → G ⊆ U → μ G ≤ liminf (fun j => μs j G) atTop) → ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ U → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, f x ∂(μs j)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂μ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the last sentence of Simon's proof of 7.2.4 (chapter-07.txt lines 284–289: from (13), (14) “it now easily follows (by a standard approximation argument) that ∫ f dμ_{T_j} → ∫ f dμ_T”); step 9 of the parent proof. Details:
1. Let C := tsupport f, a compact subset of U. By (a), μ(C) < ∞; by (b), limsup_j μ_j(C) ≤ μ(C) < ∞, so there are j₀ ∈ ℕ and Λ < ∞ with μ_j(C) ≤ Λ for all j ≥ j₀. Every bounded Borel function vanishing outside C is integrable for μ and for every μ_j with j ≥ j₀. Since convergence of a sequence depends only on its tail, only j ≥ j₀ is considered below.
2. Write f = f⁺ − f⁻ with f^± := max(±f, 0): continuous, nonnegative, vanishing outside C, and ∫ f dν = ∫ f⁺ dν − ∫ f⁻ dν for ν ∈ {μ} ∪ {μ_j : j ≥ j₀}. So it suffices to prove ∫ g dμ_j → ∫ g dμ for a continuous g ≥ 0 vanishing outside C. Let b := max g; if b = 0 both sides vanish.
3. (Layer cake.) For ν as above, ∫ g dν = ∫_0^b ν({g > t}) dt (Cavalieri's principle, e.g. Mathlib Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt); the integrand is ≤ ν(C) < ∞ and vanishes for t ≥ b.
4. Fix t > 0. G_t := {g > t} is open and G_t ⊆ C ⊆ U; K_t := {g ≥ t} is closed and contained in C, hence compact and contained in U. The sets {g = t}, t > 0, are pairwise disjoint subsets of C and μ(C) < ∞, so D := {t > 0 : μ({g = t}) > 0} is countable. For t ∈ (0, b) ∖ D we have μ(K_t) = μ(G_t), and by (b) and (c), limsup_j μ_j(G_t) ≤ limsup_j μ_j(K_t) ≤ μ(K_t) = μ(G_t) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G_t). Hence μ_j(G_t) → μ(G_t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (0, b).
5. For j ≥ j₀ and t ∈ (0, b), 0 ≤ μ_j(G_t) ≤ μ_j(C) ≤ Λ, a constant, integrable on (0, b). By dominated convergence and step 3, ∫ g dμ_j = ∫_0^b μ_j(G_t) dt → ∫_0^b μ(G_t) dt = ∫ g dμ.
6. Applying step 5 to g = f⁺ and to g = f⁻ and subtracting gives ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Eventual finiteness: μ_j(spt f) ≤ Λ for large j and μ(spt f) < ∞; reduce to f ≥ 0 via f = f⁺ − f⁻.
Layer cake: ∫ g dν = ∫_0^b ν({g > t}) dt.
For all but countably many t, the open set {g > t} and the compact set {g ≥ t} have the same μ-measure, so (b), (c) give μ_j({g > t}) → μ({g > t}); conclude by dominated convergence.

subproblem.title: Slicing of currents with representations by Lipschitz functions: support and mass inequalities (Simon Ch. 6, 4.6–4.10)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), and suppose T and ∂T are represented by measures: there are Borel measures μ, μ' on ℝ^P, finite on compact subsets of U, and a.e. strongly measurable fields ξ (of (k+1)-vectors), ξ' (of k-vectors) with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ'-a.e. x (Euclidean coefficient norm), T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω) dμ for ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and ∂T(η) = ∫ξ'(η) dμ' for η ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be Lipschitz with constant L. Then there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ' (Simon's T⌞{f < t} and (∂T)⌞{f < t}), such that the slice Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t satisfies: (∂A_t)(η) = B_t(η), i.e. Z_t(η) = 0, whenever η ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and tsupport η is disjoint from {f = t}; for every open W and t, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0⁺} h⁻¹ μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}); and for every open W and a, b ∈ ℝ, the lower integral ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(Z_t) dt ≤ L · μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (k + 1)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ' K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ' μ' → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (k + 1), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ', ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ' x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1), T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ η : TestFormOn U k, T.boundary η = ∫ x, ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') → LipschitzWith L f → ∃ (A : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (B : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn U k), (∀ (t : ℝ) (ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1)), A t ω = ∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (η : TestFormOn U k), B t η = ∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (η : TestFormOn U k), Disjoint (tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) {x | f x = t} → (A t).boundary η = B t η) ∧ (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (t : ℝ), IsOpen W → ((A t).boundary - B t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ (W ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) ∧ (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (a b : ℝ), IsOpen W → ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, ((A t).boundary - B t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * μ (W ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.6–4.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 1324–1404, printed pp. 157–158): slices of a current T with M_W(T) + M_W(∂T) < ∞ by a Lipschitz function f, defined by 4.6 ⟨T, f, t₋⟩ := ∂(T⌞{f < t}) − (∂T)⌞{f < t}, the support property 4.8 and the mass inequalities 4.9–4.10. Simon proves 4.8–4.9 for f ∈ C¹ via 4.11 and says “to handle general Lipschitz f we simply use f^{(σ)} in place of f … then let σ ↓ 0”; that limiting argument is written out in step 3. Here the restrictions are taken with respect to the given representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T, which is Simon's 2.9 (T⌞A(ω) = ∫_A ⟨ω, T⃗⟩ dμ_T) for any representation; A_t := T⌞{f < t}, B_t := (∂T)⌞{f < t}, Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t (= ⟨T, f, t₋⟩).

Notation: |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector (covectorEuclideanNorm); |ω|_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)|. Elementary facts: (E1) for a 1-covector β and a k-covector γ, |β ∧ γ| ≤ |β||γ| (k!|γ|² = Σ_{i_1,…,i_k} γ(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_k})² is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear form γ, independent of the orthonormal basis, so |·| is invariant under orthogonal changes of coordinates; rotate so that β = |β|e¹, then β∧γ = |β|Σ_{I∌1}γ_I e¹∧e^I); (E2) by hypothesis |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ'-a.e. x.

Proof.
1. (The restricted currents exist.) For a Borel set E define A_E(ω) := ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U). By (E2), |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω|_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}(x) μ-a.e., and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so μ(tsupport ω) < ∞ and the integrand is integrable (it is a.e. strongly measurable as the composition of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ with the continuous pairing). A_E is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^{k+1}(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U, uniform convergence of the forms and of all derivatives; |·| is equivalent to any norm on the finite-dimensional covector space), then |A_E(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ μ(K) → 0. So A_E ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U). Likewise B_E(η) := ∫_E ξ'(η) dμ' defines B_E ∈ 𝒟_k(U). Put A_t := A_{{f<t}}, B_t := B_{{f<t}} ({f < t} is open, f being continuous). These satisfy the first two conclusions. Note also T = A_{ℝ^P} and ∂T = B_{ℝ^P} by the representation hypotheses.

2. (Support of the slice.) Let η ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅. K := tsupport η is compact, so K = K₋ ∪ K₊ with K₋ := K ∩ {f < t} and K₊ := K ∩ {f > t} disjoint compact sets. Choose χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K₋ and χ = 0 on a neighbourhood of K₊, and put η₋ := χη, η₊ := (1 − χ)η. Both are test forms in U, η = η₋ + η₊, and since η₋ vanishes near K₊ and outside K, tsupport η₋ ⊆ K₋ ⊆ {f < t}; similarly tsupport η₊ ⊆ K₊ ⊆ {f > t}. Then:
 (∂A_t)(η₊) = A_t(dη₊) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(dη₊) dμ = 0 and B_t(η₊) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η₊) dμ' = 0, because η₊ and dη₊ vanish on {f < t};
 (∂A_t)(η₋) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(dη₋) dμ = ∫ ξ(dη₋) dμ = T(dη₋) = ∂T(η₋) = ∫ ξ'(η₋) dμ' = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η₋) dμ' = B_t(η₋), because η₋ and dη₋ vanish outside {f < t}.
Adding, (A_t).boundary η = B_t η, the third conclusion.

3. (Pointwise estimate, Simon 4.9 for Lipschitz f.) Fix t ∈ ℝ and an open W. Let 0 < h < 1 and ε := h²/8. Choose a C^∞ nonincreasing γ : ℝ → [0, 1] with γ = 1 on (−∞, t − h + ε], γ = 0 on [t − ε, ∞) and |γ'| ≤ 1/(h − 4ε) (mollify, at scale < ε, the piecewise linear function equal to 1 on (−∞, t − h + 2ε], to 0 on [t − 2ε, ∞) and linear in between). Let f_σ := f ∗ φ_σ (σ > 0, φ_σ a standard mollifier on ℝ^P): f_σ is C^∞, |∇f_σ| ≤ L everywhere and |f_σ − f| ≤ Lσ. For σ with Lσ < ε put g_σ := γ ∘ f_σ (C^∞, values in [0, 1], all derivatives bounded on compact sets) and g := γ ∘ f (continuous).
 (i) For η ∈ 𝒟^k(U): g_σ dη and g_ση are test forms in U and d(g_σ η) = dg_σ ∧ η + g_σ dη, so
 T(g_σ dη) − ∂T(g_σ η) = T(g_σ dη) − T(d(g_σ η)) = −T(dg_σ ∧ η).
 (ii) dg_σ(x) = γ'(f_σ(x)) df_σ(x) vanishes unless t − h + ε < f_σ(x) < t − ε, and then t − h < f(x) < t (as |f_σ − f| < ε); |dg_σ| ≤ L/(h − 4ε). By the representation of T, (E1) and (E2): if tsupport η ⊆ W and |η| ≤ 1, then |T(dg_σ ∧ η)| ≤ ∫ |dg_σ||η| dμ ≤ (L/(h − 4ε)) μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}).
 (iii) As σ ↓ 0, g_σ → g uniformly (γ is Lipschitz and f_σ → f uniformly), so by the representations, T(g_σ dη) → ∫ g ξ(dη) dμ and ∂T(g_σ η) → ∫ g ξ'(η) dμ' (dominated convergence on the compact set tsupport η, of finite μ- and μ'-measure). Hence for admissible η (tsupport η ⊆ W, |η| ≤ 1):
 ∫ g_h ξ(dη) dμ − ∫ g_h ξ'(η) dμ' ≤ (L/(h(1 − h/2))) μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}), where g_h := γ_h ∘ f records the dependence of γ on h, and h − 4ε = h(1 − h/2).
 (iv) As h ↓ 0, g_h → 1_{{f<t}} pointwise: if f(x) < t then f(x) ≤ t − h + ε for h ≤ t − f(x), so g_h(x) = 1; if f(x) ≥ t then f(x) ≥ t − ε and g_h(x) = 0. By dominated convergence, ∫ g_h ξ(dη) dμ → ∫_{f<t} ξ(dη) dμ = (∂A_t)(η) and ∫ g_h ξ'(η) dμ' → B_t(η). Taking the limit along a sequence h_i ↓ 0 realizing liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) (and using (1 − h/2)⁻¹ → 1) gives
 Z_t(η) = (∂A_t − B_t)(η) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t})
for every admissible η. Hence M_W(Z_t) = sup ofReal(Z_t(η)) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0⁺} ofReal(h⁻¹) μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) in [0, ∞], the fourth conclusion. (All inequalities in (ii)–(iv) may be read in [0, ∞]; the integrals involved are finite because only the compact set tsupport η matters, e.g. μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) may be replaced by μ(tsupport η ∩ {t − h < f < t}) < ∞ in (ii). If L = 0 then f is constant, {t − h < f < t} = ∅ for small h, the bound in (ii) is 0 and Z_t = 0; so the ℝ≥0∞ convention 0·∞ = 0 causes no problem: when the liminf is ∞ we have L > 0 and the claim is trivial.)

4. (Integral estimate, Simon 4.10.) Fix an open W and a, b. If a ≥ b then Ioo a b = ∅ and there is nothing to prove; assume a < b. If L = 0, step 3 gives M_W(Z_t) = 0 for every t and the claim holds. If L > 0 and μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise let F(s) := μ(W ∩ {a < f < s}) for s ≤ b and F(s) := F(b) for s > b: a bounded nondecreasing real function on ℝ with F = 0 on (−∞, a]. For t ∈ (a, b) and 0 < h < t − a, {t − h < f < t} ⊆ {a < f < t} ∖ {a < f < t − h}, so μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) ≤ F(t) − F(t − h). By Lebesgue's theorem (Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt), F is differentiable at a.e. t, and there step 3 gives M_W(Z_t) ≤ L F'(t). Hence (Mathlib lintegral_mono_ae; the lower Lebesgue integral needs no measurability of t ↦ M_W(Z_t)) ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(Z_t) dt ≤ L ∫⁻_{(a,b)} F'(t) dt. Finally ∫_{(a,b)} F' ≤ F(b) − F(a) = μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) by Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc (F' = deriv F a.e. is nonnegative, it is integrable on [a, b] by Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv, and its interval integral lies in [0, F(b) − F(a)]); F(a) = 0. This is the fifth conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: The restricted currents exist (integrable integrands, sequential continuity from finiteness of μ, μ′ on compacts).
Support: split a test form disjoint from {f = t} into parts supported in {f < t} and {f > t}; on each part ∂A_t and B_t agree.
Pointwise bound: smooth cut-offs γ ∘ f_σ (f_σ a mollification of f) give ∂(T⌞g) − (∂T)⌞g = −T⌞(dg ∧ ·) with mass ≤ (L/h)μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}); let σ → 0 and h → 0.

subproblem.title: Deformation theorem for integer multiplicity currents with a finite set of approximating currents (Simon Ch. 6, 5.1–5.4)
subproblem.statement: For all P, m ∈ ℕ (degree n := m + 1) there is a constant c ∈ ℝ≥0 with c ≥ 1 such that for every ρ > 0, every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and every Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 there is a finite set 𝒬 of currents in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with the following property. If T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, spt T ⊆ K, M(T) ≤ Λ and M(∂T) < ∞, then there are Q ∈ 𝒬, R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that: Q, ∂Q and R are integer multiplicity; T − Q − S = ∂R; Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρⁿ; M(Q) ≤ c·M(T), M(∂Q) ≤ c·M(∂T), M(R) ≤ c·ρ·M(T) and M(S) ≤ c·ρ·M(∂T); spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ thickening(3√P·ρ, spt T) and spt ∂Q ∪ spt S ⊆ thickening(3√P·ρ, spt ∂T), where thickening(r, A) := {x : |x − y| < r for some y ∈ A} (Mathlib Metric.thickening; it is empty when A = ∅). Here M := massOn ℝ^P is the total mass (GeometricCurrentOn.mass, with the Euclidean coefficient norm), masses and products are read in [0, ∞], and spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Nothing beyond these properties is asserted about Q: in particular the statement does not assert that Q is a polyhedral chain (that is only a feature of the construction used in the proof).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), ∃ c : NNReal, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ (ρ : ℝ) (K : Set (Euclid P)) (Λ : NNReal), 0 < ρ → IsCompact K → ∃ 𝒬 : Set (GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), 𝒬.Finite ∧ ∀ T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity T → T.support ⊆ K → T.mass ≤ Λ → T.boundary.mass < ∞ → ∃ Q ∈ 𝒬, ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity Q ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity Q.boundary ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ T - Q - S = R.boundary ∧ (Q = 0 ∨ ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ (m + 1)) ≤ Q.mass) ∧ Q.mass ≤ c * T.mass ∧ Q.boundary.mass ≤ c * T.boundary.mass ∧ R.mass ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal ρ * T.mass ∧ S.mass ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal ρ * T.boundary.mass ∧ Q.support ∪ R.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * ρ) T.support ∧ Q.boundary.support ∪ S.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * ρ) T.boundary.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, §5 (Deformation Theorem 5.1, scaled version 5.3, Lemma 5.4 and the proof (1)–(38), chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928, printed pp. 158–168), with the tools it cites: homotopy formula and mass estimate 2.25–2.29 (lines 440–530), slicing 4.6–4.10, integrality of push-forwards 3.3–3.9, completeness 3.13 and the BV facts 2.34–2.37 and Ch. 2, 2.7, 2.9 used on the faces. Where Simon cites a result whose proof is not in the pinned library, the argument is given below (Parts A–C); the main proof (Parts D–E) is Simon's printed proof with details filled in. Departures: (i) Simon's 3.13 (completeness) is replaced by the direct integral representation of the push-forwards (B3–B4), which shows integrality without passing to limits of integer multiplicity currents; (ii) the BV structure of the face densities (Simon's appeal to 2.35 and Ch. 2, 2.7, 2.9) is replaced by the integer multiplicity structure of Q plus the elementary Poincaré and trace inequalities of C1–C2; (iii) the printed constant “|y − a| ≥ 3/4” in the proof of 5.4 is corrected to |y − a| ≥ 1/4 (a ∈ B_{1/4}(q), y ∈ ∂C), which only changes constants; (iv) the support radius 2√P ρ of the statement is used in the slightly weaker form 3√P ρ (the face-replacement step (E7) moves supports by up to √n ρ more), which is what the Lean statement asserts. Scope of the statement: the conclusion asserts only that Q lies in the finite set 𝒬 and has the listed integrality, mass and support properties. That the Q constructed below is a polyhedral chain Σ_F β_F[[F]] on the cubical grid of side ρ with integer coefficients β_F is a property of this construction; it is used inside the proof (E0) to define the finite set 𝒬 and to obtain the dichotomy Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρⁿ, and it is not part of the conclusion.

Notation and conventions. n := m + 1 ≥ 1 is the degree. IM := integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity). All currents in this proof live in ℝ^P (domain univ) or ℝ × ℝ^P; M(X) := M_{ℝ^P}(X) = X.mass; |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector, |ω|_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)|; for a k-vector ζ (continuous linear functional on k-covectors) |ζ| := sup{⟨α, ζ⟩ : |α| ≤ 1} (dual norm). For currents X, Y, X + Y := X − (0 − Y). The zero current (in any degree) is IM: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents the zero current (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero; the positivity, integrability, measurability and orientation fields hold vacuously because μHE restricted to ∅ is the zero measure; and the representing integral over ∅ is 0); this is used whenever Q, R or S is taken to be 0. Siblings used: vanish_off_support (VO), mass_equals_rep_measure (MR), mass_representation (REP: representation (μ_X, ξ_X) with μ_X(G) = M_G(X), |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α|, and absolute continuity μ_X ≪ Hᵏ for X with M + M∂ locally finite), im_calculus (IMC: locality of approximate tangent spaces, IM restrictions, differences), slicing (SL). For X with compact support and finite mass, (VO) and (REP) give μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ spt X) = 0, so μ_X is a finite measure with compact support, and |X(ω)| ≤ ∫ |ω| dμ_X. For a Borel set B and a bounded Borel g, X⌞B(ω) := ∫_B ξ_X(ω) dμ_X and X⌞g(ω) := ∫ g ξ_X(ω) dμ_X are currents (linear; sequentially continuous because |X⌞g(ω)| ≤ sup|g|·|ω|_∞·μ_X(tsupport ω)) with M(X⌞g) ≤ ∫ |g| dμ_X, and X⌞g(ω) = X(gω) for smooth g; for IM X these agree with the IM restrictions of IMC(b) (both represent the same vector measure on test forms, hence on bounded Borel functions).

Multilinear algebra used throughout (Euclidean norms).
(L0) For a k-covector β on ℝ^P, k!|β|² = Σ_{i_1,…,i_k} β(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_k})² =: ‖β‖²_HS (alternating: each increasing tuple appears k! times up to sign, tuples with repeats vanish). ‖·‖_HS is invariant under orthogonal changes of basis (it is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear form), hence so is |·|; and the dual norm on k-vectors is invariant as well.
(L1) For a linear map A : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q and a k-covector β on ℝ^Q, |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k |β|; dually |Λ_k A ζ| ≤ ‖A‖^k |ζ| for k-vectors ζ, where ⟨β, Λ_kAζ⟩ := ⟨A^#β, ζ⟩. Proof: by (L0) it suffices to bound ‖·‖_HS; replacing one slot of a multilinear form γ by A multiplies its Hilbert–Schmidt norm by at most ‖A‖ (for fixed other arguments, Σ_i γ(Ae_i, …)² = |Aᵀg|² ≤ ‖A‖²|g|², g the vector representing γ(·, …)); do this k times.
(L2) For a 1-covector β' and a k-covector γ, |β' ∧ γ| ≤ |β'||γ|: by (L0) rotate so that β' = |β'|e¹; then β' ∧ γ = |β'| Σ_{I∌1} γ_I e¹ ∧ e^I. Dually |v ∧ ζ| ≤ |v||ζ| for a vector v and a k-vector ζ, where ⟨β, v ∧ ζ⟩ := ⟨ι_vβ, ζ⟩ (and |ι_vβ| ≤ |v||β| likewise).
(L3) If τ_1, …, τ_k are orthonormal then ζ := τ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_k (⟨α, ζ⟩ := α(τ_1, …, τ_k)) has |ζ| = 1 (by (L0) rotate so that τ_i = e_i; then ⟨α, ζ⟩ = α(e_1, …, e_k) is one coordinate of α). If A : ℝ^k → ℝ^P is linear and injective, write A = O S (polar decomposition: S := (AᵀA)^{1/2}, O := AS⁻¹ an isometric embedding); then Λ_kA(e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_k) = det(S)·Oe_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ Oe_k, so |Λ_kA(e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_k)| = det S = √det(AᵀA) =: JA and Λ_kA(e)/JA is a unit simple k-vector orienting A(ℝ^k); if A is not injective, Λ_kA(e) = 0 = JA. Two unit simple k-vectors orienting the same k-plane differ by a sign (change of orthonormal basis has determinant ±1). Also, by IMC(d), the orientation of an IMRep satisfies |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| a.e.

Part A. Calculus of normal currents with compact support.
A1 (Smooth push-forward; Simon 2.23–2.24.) Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) have compact support and F : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be C^∞. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^Q) let (F^#ω)(x)(v_1, …, v_k) := ω(F(x))(DF(x)v_1, …, DF(x)v_k) (Lean: (ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)), a smooth k-form, and F_#X(ω) := X(ζ F^#ω) with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) equal to 1 near spt X; by (VO) this does not depend on ζ. F_#X is a current (if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^Q) then ζF^#ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) by the chain and Leibniz rules), ∂F_#X = F_#∂X (d commutes with F^# — SimonGMT Chapter06 exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin — and X(dζ ∧ F^#ω) = 0 by (VO)), and spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X). If M(X) < ∞, then F_#X(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω(F(x)), Λ_k DF(x) ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X(x), so by (L1) M(F_#X) ≤ ∫ ‖DF‖^k dμ_X ≤ sup_{spt X} ‖DF‖^k M(X).
A2 (Product with [[0,1]]; Simon 2.17–2.21.) Write points of ℝ × ℝ^P as (t, x) and e₀ := ∂_t. For an (k+1)-form ω on ℝ × ℝ^P let ω₁(t, x) be the k-covector on ℝ^P given by ω₁(t,x)(v_1, …, v_k) := ω(t,x)(e₀, (0,v_1), …, (0,v_k)) and ω₀ the “dt-free part”. For X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) with compact support define ([[0,1]] × X)(ω) := X(∫_0^1 ω₁(t, ·) dt) (the integrand is a smooth compactly supported k-form on ℝ^P), and ({s} × X)(ω) := X(i_s^#ω), i_s(x) := (s, x). These are currents in ℝ × ℝ^P with compact support. Writing ω = dt ∧ ω₁ + ω₀, d(dt ∧ ω₁) = −dt ∧ d_xω₁ and dω₀ = dt ∧ ∂_tω₀ + d_xω₀, so (dω)₁ = ∂_tω₀ − d_xω₁; integrating in t and using that d_x commutes with ∫dt gives
 ∂([[0,1]] × X) = {1} × X − {0} × X − [[0,1]] × ∂X (for k ≥ 1; for k = 0 the last term is absent).
If M(X) < ∞ then ([[0,1]] × X)(ω) = ∫_0^1 ∫ ⟨ω(t,x), e₀ ∧ ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X dt and M([[0,1]] × X) ≤ M(X).
A3 (Homotopy formula and estimate; Simon 2.25–2.27.) For C^∞ maps F, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q let H(t, x) := F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)). Since ∂H_# = H_#∂ and H ∘ i_1 = G, H ∘ i_0 = F, A2 gives
 G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#([[0,1]] × X) + H_#([[0,1]] × ∂X) (last term absent for k = 0).
If M(X) < ∞: DH(t,x)e₀ = G(x) − F(x) and DH(t,x)(0, v) = ((1 − t)DF(x) + tDG(x))v, so Λ_{k+1}DH(e₀ ∧ ζ) = (G − F)(x) ∧ Λ_k((1−t)DF + tDG)(x)ζ and by (L1), (L2)
 M(H_#([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ ∫ |G − F| (‖DF‖ + ‖DG‖)^k dμ_X ≤ sup_{spt X}|G − F| · sup_{spt X}(‖DF‖ + ‖DG‖)^k · M(X).
A4 (Lipschitz push-forward; Simon 2.29.) Let X have compact support with M(X) + M(∂X) < ∞ (k ≥ 1; for k = 0 drop the ∂X terms) and F : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be Lipschitz with constant Λ. F_σ := F ∗ φ_σ (componentwise mollification) is C^∞, ‖DF_σ‖ ≤ Λ, F_σ → F uniformly. By A3 for F_σ, F_τ,
 |(F_σ)_#X(ω) − (F_τ)_#X(ω)| ≤ sup|F_σ − F_τ| ((2Λ)^k M(X)|dω|_∞ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)|ω|_∞) → 0,
so F_#X(ω) := lim_{σ↓0}(F_σ)_#X(ω) exists. Properties: (a) |F_#X(ω)| ≤ Λ^k M(X)|ω|_∞, so F_#X is a current and M(F_#X) ≤ Λ^k M(X); (b) ∂F_#X = F_#∂X; (c) for smooth F it agrees with A1 (DF_σ → DF uniformly on compact sets); (d) spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X) (if spt ω ∩ F(spt X) = ∅ then spt ω ∩ F_σ(spt X) = ∅ for small σ); (e) if F, G are Lipschitz (constants ≤ Λ) and |F − G| ≤ δ on spt X, then |F_#X(ω) − G_#X(ω)| ≤ δ((2Λ)^k M(X)|dω|_∞ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)|ω|_∞) (pass to the limit in A3); in particular F_#X depends only on F|spt X, so for a map ψ that is Lipschitz on a closed set A ⊇ spt X, ψ_#X := (ψ̃)_#X is well defined for any Lipschitz extension ψ̃ of ψ|A (componentwise McShane extension, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real, constant ≤ √Q Lip(ψ|A)), and linear in X among currents supported in A; (f) homotopy formula: for Lipschitz F, G, with H(t,x) := F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) (Lipschitz on [0,1] × ℝ^P when G − F is bounded, extended to t ∉ [0,1] by clamping), G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#([[0,1]] × X) + H_#([[0,1]] × ∂X) and M(H_#([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ sup_{spt X}|G − F|·(Lip F + Lip G)^k M(X), similarly for ∂X with exponent k − 1 (apply A3 to F_σ, G_σ with the homotopies H_σ(t, x) := F_σ(x) + s(t)(G_σ − F_σ)(x), where s ∈ C^∞(ℝ) is bounded with s(t) = t on [−1, 2] (only [0,1] × spt X matters, so A3 holds verbatim with s in place of t); the H_σ are globally Lipschitz with bounded constants and converge uniformly to H(t, x) := F(x) + s(t)(G − F)(x), so by (e) applied in ℝ × ℝ^P and lower semicontinuity of mass, SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf, the identity and the estimate pass to the limit).

Part B. Integrality of Lipschitz push-forwards (Simon 3.3–3.9 and 3.2(2)).
Throughout X = τ(M, θ, ξ) is an IM k-current in ℝ^P (k ≥ 1) with compact support and M(∂X) < ∞; by (MR) and (IMC) we may assume M ⊆ spt X, so Hᵏ(M) ≤ ∫_M θ dHᵏ = M(X) < ∞. Lebesgue measure on ℝᵏ is Lᵏ, Hᵏ = μHE[k].
B1 (Parametrization.) There are countably many compact sets A_i ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz G_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ^P and κ_i > 0 such that: G_i is differentiable at every u ∈ A_i with DG_i(u) injective; |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| ≥ κ_i|u − v| for u, v ∈ A_i; the sets G_i(A_i) ⊆ M are pairwise disjoint; Hᵏ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0. Moreover, given an open set O with Hᵏ(M ∖ O) = 0 and a countable family of compact sets whose interiors cover O, the construction may be run on M ∩ O, so that Hᵏ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0 still holds and each G_i(A_i) lies inside one member of the family.
Proof. By definition (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable) M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝᵏ) with Hᵏ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz. By Rademacher (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) the set D_j of differentiability points of F_j is Borel with null complement, and Hᵏ(F_j(ℝᵏ ∖ D_j)) = 0 (Lipschitz images of null sets are null, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). On Z_j := {u ∈ D_j : DF_j(u) not injective} the Jacobian vanishes, so Hᵏ(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT Chapter02 area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero). Let E_j := (D_j ∖ Z_j) ∩ F_j^{-1}(M) (Borel). For injective A choose an antilipschitz constant K_A > 0 (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith: |Au| ≥ |u|/K_A) and put r(A) := 1/(2K_A); r(A) := 1 for non-injective A. (absolutely convergent; JH_i = |Λ_kDH_i(e)| = |Λ_k(d^MF)(Λ_kDG_i(e))| = J^MF(G_iu)·JG_i(u) by (B2′)). Where DH_i(u) is not injective, Λ_kDH_i(u)(e) = 0. Part C. Top-dimensional pieces on faces.
C1 (Poincaré and trace inequalities on a cube.) Let Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ ℝⁿ, u ∈ L¹(Q₁) and V := sup{∫_{Q₁} u div g : g ∈ C_c^∞(Q₁; ℝⁿ), |g| ≤ 1} < ∞. Then (i) ∫_{Q₁} |u − β| ≤ c_n V for every median β of u (Lⁿ{u ≥ β} ≥ 1/2 and Lⁿ{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2), and (ii) the current Y := u[[Q₁]] (Y(a dy) := ∫_{Q₁} u a) on ℝⁿ satisfies M(∂Y) ≤ c_n(V + ∫_{Q₁}|u|).
Proof. For 0 < σ < δ < 1/8 let Q_δ := (δ, 1 − δ)ⁿ and u_σ := u ∗ φ_σ on Q_δ (smooth on a neighbourhood of closure Q_δ). For g ∈ C_c^∞(Q_δ; ℝⁿ), |g| ≤ 1, Fubini gives ∫ ∇u_σ·g = −∫ u div(φ̌_σ ∗ g) with φ̌_σ ∗ g ∈ C_c^∞(Q₁; ℝⁿ), |φ̌_σ ∗ g| ≤ 1, so ∫_{Q_δ}|∇u_σ| ≤ V. Smooth Poincaré on a cube Q' of side s ∈ [1/2, 1]: for v ∈ C¹(closure Q'), |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ∫_0^1|∇v(x + t(y − x))||y − x| dt; integrating over Q' × Q' and substituting z = x + t(y − x) in x for t ≤ 1/2 (Jacobian (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}) and in y for t ≥ 1/2 gives ∫∫|v(x) − v(y)| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n s^{n+1}∫|∇v|, hence ∫_{Q'}|v − v_{Q'}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n ∫_{Q'}|∇v|. Smooth trace inequality: on the face {x₁ = δ} of Q_δ, |v(δ, x')| ≤ |v(x₁, x')| + ∫|∂₁v(t, x')| dt; averaging over x₁ (length ≥ 1/2) and integrating over x' gives ∫_{face}|v| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|v| + ∫_{Q_δ}|∇v|, so ∫_{∂Q_δ}|v| ≤ 2n(2∫_{Q_δ}|v| + ∫_{Q_δ}|∇v|). Apply these to v = u_σ: u_σ → u in L¹(Q_δ) as σ ↓ 0 (continuity of translations in L¹: ‖u ∗ φ_σ − u‖ ≤ sup_{|h|≤σ}‖u(· − h) − u‖, approximate u by continuous compactly supported functions), so ∫_{Q_δ}|u − u_{Q_δ}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V; letting δ ↓ 0 (u_{Q_δ} → u_{Q₁}, monotone convergence) gives ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V, and (i) follows because a median minimizes c ↦ ∫|u − c|. For (ii), the divergence theorem on Q_δ gives, for γ = Σ g_jε_j with |g| ≤ 1 (ε_j := (−1)^{j−1}dy¹∧⋯∧dy^{j−1}∧dy^{j+1}∧⋯∧dyⁿ, dγ = (div g)dy), |∂(u_σ[[Q_δ]])(γ)| = |∫_{Q_δ} u_σ div g| ≤ ∫_{Q_δ}|∇u_σ| + ∫_{∂Q_δ}|u_σ| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|u_σ|; as δ ↓ 0, σ = σ(δ) ↓ 0, u_σ1_{Q_δ} → u1_{Q₁} in L¹, so u_σ[[Q_δ]] ⇀ Y, and lower semicontinuity of mass gives M(∂Y) ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|u|. ∎
C2 (Integer-valued medians.) If u is integer-valued, β := min{c ∈ ℤ : Lⁿ{u ≤ c} ≥ 1/2} is a median, and |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u| (if β > 0 then Lⁿ{u ≥ β} ≥ 1/2, so ∫|u| ≥ β/2; similarly if β < 0); if u is a.e. equal to a constant c then β = c.

Part D. The retraction (Simon 5.4). Notation of Simon §5 (unit grid): ℓ := P − n ≥ 1 (the case ℓ = 0 is treated in E0), C := [0,1]^P, q := (1/2, …, 1/2), L_j := j-skeleton of the unit cubical decomposition, S_1, …, S_N (N = binom(P, n+1)) the (n+1)-dimensional coordinate subspaces, p_j the orthogonal projection onto S_j, F_j := C ∩ S_j, x_j := p_j(q). For a ∈ B_{1/4}(q), the dual skeleton is L*(a) := ⋃_{j=1}^N ⋃_{z ∈ ℤ^P ∩ S_j} p_j^{-1}(p_j(a) + z) = a + L_{ℓ−1} (a point lies in L_{ℓ−1} iff at least n + 1 of its coordinates are integers), L*(a; ρ) := {x : dist(x, L*(a)) < ρ} = ⋃_j ⋃_z p_j^{-1}(B_ρ(p_j(a) + z)), and dist(L*(a), L_n) ≥ 1/4 (a point of L_n has at least ℓ integer coordinates, a point of L*(a) has at least n + 1 coordinates in a + ℤ ⊆ (1/4, 3/4) + ℤ, and n + 1 + ℓ > P).
Lemma D. There is a map ψ : ℝ^P ∖ L*(a) → L_n with ψ = id on L_n, ψ(z + x) = z + ψ(x) (z ∈ ℤ^P), ψ(z + C ∖ L*(a)) ⊆ z + C (so |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P), and pointwise upper Lipschitz constant D̄ψ(x) := limsup_{y→x}|ψ(y) − ψ(x)|/|y − x| ≤ c₁/dist(x, L*(a)), c₁ = c₁(n, P). Consequently, for 0 < ρ ≤ 1/4, ψ is Lipschitz on {d ≥ ρ} (d := dist(·, L*(a))) with constant c₂/ρ, c₂ := 2c₁ + 8√P + 1.
Proof (Simon's, with details). For each j-face F of C with j ≥ n + 1 let a_F be the orthogonal projection of a onto the affine hull of F (its free coordinates are those of a, in (1/4, 3/4), so a_F ∈ F) and ψ_F : F ∖ {a_F} → ∂F the radial retraction from a_F (ψ_F = id on ∂F). Faces shared by neighbouring cubes get the same a_F (the free coordinates are unchanged by the lattice translation), so ψ^{(j)} := ⋃_F ψ_F (over j-faces F) is a well defined continuous map from ⋃_F (F ∖ {a_F}) to the (j−1)-skeleton. (1) L*(a) ∩ F = ⋃_{ℓ' ∈ J_F} (p_{ℓ'}^{-1}(p_{ℓ'}(a)) ∩ F), J_F := {ℓ' : S_{ℓ'} spanned by n + 1 free coordinates of F}: a plane p_{ℓ'}^{-1}(p_{ℓ'}(a) + z) meets F only if its n + 1 prescribed coordinates are free coordinates of F (a fixed coordinate of F is 0 or 1 ∉ a_i + ℤ) and then z = 0 in those coordinates. Each of these planes contains a_F (a_F − a is orthogonal to the free directions). Hence L*(a) ∩ F is a union of affine subspaces of aff(F) through a_F, i.e. a cone with vertex a_F, so ψ_F maps F ∖ L*(a) into ∂F ∖ L*(a). Therefore ψ₀ := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P)} is defined on C ∖ L*(a), with values in C ∩ L_n, equal to the identity on C ∩ L_n, and ψ(z + x) := z + ψ₀(x) is well defined on ℝ^P ∖ L*(a) (on common faces of neighbouring cubes the definitions agree). Bound (3) by induction on ℓ. For ℓ = 1, L*(a) ∩ C = {a}, ψ is the radial projection from a onto ∂C on C, and D̄ψ(x) ≤ c/|x − a| ≤ c/dist(x, L*(a)) (|y − a| ≤ √P for y ∈ ∂C, |x − a| ≥ dist(x, L*(a))). For ℓ ≥ 2, let x ∈ int C ∖ L*(a), y := ψ^{(P)}(x) ∈ ∂C the radial projection from a, F a closed (P−1)-face of C containing y, p_F the orthogonal projection onto aff(F) (so p_F(a) = a_F), and L := L*(a) ∩ aff(F), which by (1) is the dual skeleton of the (P−1)-dimensional cube F with centre a_F (codimension ℓ − 1). Split L = L₀ ∪ L₁, where L₀ consists of the planes of L through a_F (those of (1)) and L₁ of the remaining (periodically translated) planes, each of which lies at distance ≥ 1/4 from F (a prescribed free coordinate a_i + z_i with z_i ≠ 0 differs by ≥ 1/4 from every value in [0, 1]). Since y − a = λ(x − a) with λ := |y − a|/|x − a|, and p_F^{-1}(L₀) is a cone with vertex a contained in L*(a) (it is L₀ plus the normal line of F through its points; the normal line through a lies in some p_{ℓ'}^{-1}(p_{ℓ'}(a)) because n + 1 ≤ P − 1), we get dist(y, L₀) = dist(y, p_F^{-1}(L₀)) = λ dist(x, p_F^{-1}(L₀)) ≥ λ dist(x, L*(a)) =: λd(x). As λd(x) ≤ λ|x − a| = |y − a| ≤ √P, dist(y, L) ≥ min(λd(x), 1/4) ≥ λd(x)/(4√P). The induction hypothesis for ψ̃ := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P−1)} on F gives D̄ψ̃(y) ≤ c/dist(y, L) ≤ 4√P c|x − a|/(|y − a| dist(x, L*(a))) ≤ 16√P c|x − a|/dist(x, L*(a)) (|y − a| ≥ 1/4; Simon prints 3/4), and D̄ψ^{(P)}(x) ≤ c'/|x − a|. By the chain rule for upper Lipschitz constants, D̄ψ(x) ≤ D̄ψ̃(y)D̄ψ^{(P)}(x) ≤ c₁/dist(x, L*(a)). Points of ∂C ∖ L*(a) and of other cubes are handled by periodicity and the same estimate on each closed cube. Finally, if x, y ∈ {d ≥ ρ} and |x − y| < ρ/2, the segment [x, y] lies in {d ≥ ρ/2}, where D̄ψ ≤ 2c₁/ρ, so |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ (2c₁/ρ)|x − y|; if |x − y| ≥ ρ/2, |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ 2√P + |x − y| ≤ (4√P/ρ + 1)|x − y| ≤ (c₂/ρ)|x − y|. ∎

Part E. Proof of the theorem.
E0 (Reductions.) If n > P all n- and (n+1)-currents vanish (no nonzero covectors), so T = 0 and Q = R = S = 0 work with 𝒬 := {0}. If T = 0 (in particular if spt T = ∅, by VO) take Q = R = S = 0. If ∂T = 0 then all mass bounds below involving M(∂T) force ∂Q = 0 and S = 0 (a current of mass 0 is 0), so the support conditions relative to spt ∂T = ∅ (thickening of ∅ is ∅) hold trivially. proof_key_steps: Normal-current calculus: smooth push-forwards, the product [[0,1]]×X with ∂([[0,1]]×X) = {1}×X − {0}×X − [[0,1]]×∂X, the homotopy formula with the mass estimate, and Lipschitz push-forwards by mollification.

Faces: Poincaré and trace inequalities on cubes by mollification; integer medians.
Simon 5.4: the retraction ψ onto the n-skeleton with Lipschitz constant c/dist(·, dual skeleton), with the cone property corrected for periodic planes.

Simon's proof: a good centre a by the 5-times covering lemma, good slicing radii, dyadic shells, Cauchy-in-mass limits Q₀, R₁, S₁ with T − Q₀ = ∂R₁ + S₁, integrality of Q₀ and R₁ from the integral formula, face replacement Q₀ ↦ P = Σβ_F[[F]], then scaling and the finite net 𝒬 (the polyhedral form of P is used only inside the proof, to make 𝒬 finite and to get Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρⁿ).

subproblem.title: The minimality inequality propagates from a neighbourhood of spt(S − T) to larger open sets
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, S, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity, K ⊆ ℝ^P compact with spt(S − T) ⊆ K, and W, W' ⊆ ℝ^P open with K ⊆ W ⊆ W' and closure(W') compact and contained in U. If M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S), then M_{W'}(T) ≤ M_{W'}(S).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (K W W' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity S → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsCompact K → (S - T).support ⊆ K → IsOpen W → IsOpen W' → K ⊆ W → W ⊆ W' → CompactlyContained W' U → T.massOn W ≤ S.massOn W → T.massOn W' ≤ S.massOn W'
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof, which supplies the details behind Simon's remark after (8) (chapter-07.txt lines 226–229: “In view of the arbitrariness of K, X this will evidently establish the fact that T is minimizing in U”).
1. Let R_S, R_T be IM representations of S and T and μ_S := R_S.measure, μ_T := R_T.measure. By the sibling lemma mass_equals_rep_measure, M_G(S) = μ_S(G) and M_G(T) = μ_T(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P. Both measures vanish outside U and are finite on compact subsets of U (local integrability of the multiplicities).
2. O := U ∖ K is open (K is compact, hence closed). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ O. Then tsupport ω ∩ spt(S − T) ⊆ O ∩ K = ∅, so (S − T)(ω) = 0 by the sibling lemma vanish_off_support; that is, S(ω) = T(ω).
3. Hence, for every open G ⊆ O, the admissible forms for M_G(S) and for M_G(T) are the same test forms (in 𝒟ⁿ(U), supported in G, of norm ≤ 1) and give the same values, so M_G(S) = M_G(T), i.e. μ_S(G) = μ_T(G) by step 1.
4. Let O_i := {x ∈ O : |x| < i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ O) > 1/i} (O_i := {|x| < i} if O = ℝ^P); these are open, increase to O, and have compact closures contained in O ⊆ U, so μ_S(O_i), μ_T(O_i) < ∞. For each i, the finite Borel measures μ_S⌞O_i and μ_T⌞O_i agree on every open set G ⊆ ℝ^P (G ∩ O_i is an open subset of O; step 3), in particular on ℝ^P; the open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra, so μ_S⌞O_i = μ_T⌞O_i (uniqueness of finite measures, e.g. Mathlib ext_of_generate_finite). For a Borel set A ⊆ O, continuity from below along O_i ↑ O gives μ_S(A) = lim_i μ_S(A ∩ O_i) = lim_i μ_T(A ∩ O_i) = μ_T(A).
5. W' ∖ W is a Borel set contained in O (W' ⊆ closure(W') ⊆ U and K ⊆ W), so μ_S(W' ∖ W) = μ_T(W' ∖ W).
6. Since W ⊆ W', μ_T(W') = μ_T(W) + μ_T(W' ∖ W) ≤ μ_S(W) + μ_S(W' ∖ W) = μ_S(W'), using μ_T(W) = M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) = μ_S(W). By step 1, M_{W'}(T) = μ_T(W') ≤ μ_S(W') = M_{W'}(S). ∎
proof_key_steps: By mass_equals_rep_measure, masses on open sets are the representation measures μ_S, μ_T.
By vanish_off_support, S and T agree on test forms supported in O = U ∖ K, so μ_S = μ_T on open subsets of O and hence (finite-measure uniqueness along an exhaustion of O) on all Borel subsets of O.
μ_T(W') = μ_T(W) + μ_T(W' ∖ W) ≤ μ_S(W) + μ_S(W' ∖ W) = μ_S(W').

audit.reason: The support lemma gives equality of current evaluations off K. The mass formula and finite-measure uniqueness transfer this equality to Borel measures there, and additive decomposition of W′ proves the exact inequality.

subproblem.title: Minimizing 0-dimensional currents vanish
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and T ∈ 𝒟_0(U) minimizing in U in the sense of the contract's IsMinimizingIn T U (Simon 7.1.1): T is integer multiplicity, and M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) for every open W with closure(W) compact and contained in U and every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_0(U) such that spt(S − T) is a compact subset of U ∩ W (the condition ∂S = ∂T is vacuous in degree 0). Then T = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U 0), IsOpen U → IsMinimizingIn T U → T = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (point removal). Simon's Ch. 6 §3 and Ch. 7 tacitly take n ≥ 1, while the contract includes n = 0.
1. (Structure in degree 0.) By hypothesis T is represented by an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U. Here H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), which gives every singleton measure 1 (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton) and is the counting measure; so a property holding H⁰-a.e. on M holds at every point of M. For compact K ⊆ U, Σ_{x∈M∩K} θ(x) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞ and θ ≥ 1 on M, so M ∩ K is finite. For each x ∈ M the orientation condition (the orthonormal family is empty) gives σ(x) ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = σ(x)·α(∅) for every 0-covector α. Consequently T(ω) = Σ_{x ∈ M ∩ tsupport ω} θ(x)σ(x)·ω(x)(∅), a finite sum.
2. Suppose T ≠ 0. Then M ≠ ∅ (if M = ∅ the defining integral vanishes for every ω). Fix x₀ ∈ M ⊆ U and r > 0 with closed ball B̄_r(x₀) ⊆ U (U is open), and let W := B_r(x₀). W is open and closure(W) = B̄_r(x₀) is compact and contained in U.
3. (Competitor.) Let M' := M ∖ {x₀} and R' := (M', θ, ξ). R' is an IMRep in U: M' is Borel and contained in U; it is countably 0-rectifiable (a subset of M); θ ≥ 1 on M'; ∫_{M'∩K} θ dH⁰ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞; ξ is H⁰⌞M'-measurable; and for x ∈ M' the approximate tangent space of M' at x is {0}, as it is for M: if f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) vanishes outside B_ρ(0), then for 0 < λ < |x₀ − x|/ρ the sets η_{x,λ}(M) ∩ B_ρ(0) and η_{x,λ}(M') ∩ B_ρ(0) coincide (η_{x,λ} is injective and (x₀ − x)/λ ∉ B_ρ(0)) and are finite, so ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M')} f dH⁰ = ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f dH⁰ → ∫_{{0}} f dH⁰ = f(0) as λ ↓ 0; thus the orientation condition of R' holds at every x ∈ M' with the same ξ(x). Define S(ω) := T(ω) − θ(x₀)σ(x₀)·ω(x₀)(∅) for ω ∈ 𝒟⁰(U). S is linear and sequentially continuous on 𝒟⁰(U) (convergence in 𝒟⁰(U) implies uniform convergence, hence convergence of ω(x₀)), so S ∈ 𝒟_0(U), and S(ω) = Σ_{x∈M'} θ(x)σ(x)·ω(x)(∅) = ∫_{M'} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH⁰. Thus R' represents S and S is integer multiplicity.
4. (Support.) (S − T)(ω) = −θ(x₀)σ(x₀)·ω(x₀)(∅). For y ∈ U ∖ {x₀} choose ρ > 0 with B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ U ∖ {x₀}; every ω ∈ 𝒟⁰(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ(y) has ω(x₀) = 0, so S − T vanishes on B_ρ(y), an open set whose closure is compact and contained in U; hence y ∉ spt(S − T). Thus spt(S − T) ⊆ {x₀}; it is compact and contained in U ∩ W.
5. (Masses.) By the sibling lemma mass_equals_rep_measure (M_G equals the representation measure on open G), M_W(T) = Σ_{x∈M∩W} θ(x), which is finite because M ∩ B̄_r(x₀) is finite, and M_W(S) = Σ_{x∈M'∩W} θ(x) = M_W(T) − θ(x₀) < M_W(T), because x₀ ∈ M ∩ W and θ(x₀) ≥ 1.
6. Steps 2–5 contradict the minimality inequality M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S). Hence T = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: In degree 0, H⁰ is counting measure: a representation is a locally finite set M with multiplicities θ ≥ 1 and signs σ, and T(ω) = Σ θσ ω(x)(∅).
If T ≠ 0, pick x₀ ∈ M and W = B_r(x₀) ⊂⊂ U; deleting x₀ gives an integer multiplicity competitor S with spt(S − T) ⊆ {x₀}.
By mass_equals_rep_measure, M_W(S) = M_W(T) − θ(x₀) < M_W(T) < ∞, contradicting minimality; so T = 0.

audit.reason: The proof correctly treats H⁰ as counting measure, verifies the point-deletion representation and competitor support, and obtains a strict finite-mass decrease. The degree-zero boundary condition is correctly vacuous.
