Neither SimonGMT nor the snapshot Mathlib has a closure, deformation, Lipschitz-slicing or flat-convergence theorem (rg: no match). These results, Riesz representation and absolute continuity of normal currents, and IM calculus therefore remain children with complete parent-written proofs. Reusable library facts: WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf and WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary, the Chapter01 Riesz, compactness, density and Lusin theorems, the Chapter02 area formulas and the Chapter03 rectifiability API. Every SimonGMT and Mathlib declaration cited by name in the child proofs exists in the pinned sources. The 451-node DAG contains no cmc_ name, and the snapshot project has no cmc_ or dtc_ name. dtc_vanish_off_support is a comparator-accepted node whose frozen type equals the vanish_off_support child type, so it is reused verbatim; accepted declarations covering parts of mass_equals_rep_measure and im_calculus are named in remarks. In the workspace build, all 12 exact child types elaborate after import GMT.Ch07.Submission. The conditional assembly of CompactnessOfMinimizingCurrents from the six used child types depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and current subtraction uses the contract instance. The identical previously accepted split was dropped only by the runtime node bound (max_nodes = 200 with about 200 DAG nodes); the current configuration allows 1000 nodes. Book lines 176–260 confirm the two corrections used in local_comparison.

subproblem.title: Federer–Fleming closure theorem and boundary rectifiability (Simon Ch. 6, 3.11 via 8.2–8.3 and 6.2–6.3)
subproblem.statement: (CL) For all P, d ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and currents T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_d(U): if every T_j is integer multiplicity, sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every open W with closure(W) compact and contained in U (∂-mass read as 0 when d = 0, contract boundaryMassOn), and T_j ⇀ T in U, then T is integer multiplicity. (BR) For all P, d ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and every integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every such W, the boundary ∂R is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P d : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U d) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U d), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + boundaryMassOn (Ts j) W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T) ∧ (∀ (P d : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : GeometricCurrentOn U (d + 1)), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity R → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → R.boundary.massOn W < ∞) → IsIntegerMultiplicity R.boundary)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 8.2 with Remarks 8.3(1),(2) (closure theorem; chapter-06.txt lines 2297–2473, printed pp. 176–179), Theorem 6.3 with 6.2 and 6.4 (boundary rectifiability; lines 1962–2003), the isoperimetric theorem 6.1 (lines 1939–1961), and Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 “⇐” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–300). Departure: Simon's proof of 8.2 obtains rectifiability from the Rectifiability Theorem 8.1, which rests on the Besicovitch–Federer structure theorem (Ch. 3, 3.6), quoted in the book without proof (“For the proof of this theorem see [Fed69] or [Ros84]”). Here 8.1 is replaced by the tangent-plane argument of B. White (Comment. Math. Helv. 64 (1989) 207–220, cf. Simon's own remark in §8 that the structure theorem can be avoided), which uses only the slices, the lower density bound proved in Simon's 8.2 and BV-type estimates proved below; integrality of the multiplicity is then read off from slices (Step V14) instead of Simon's BV compactness argument. Errata: in Simon's 8.2 proof “Θ^{*n}(μ_T, ξ) < η” may be replaced by the lower density (only a sequence of radii is needed), and the support of the isoperimetric filling must be controlled (supplied by the deformation theorem); in Ch. 3, 1.6 the constant ε = 1/16ⁿ must be taken smaller (ε := 2^{−1}16^{−n}) for the contradiction in (10).

Notation. IM := integer multiplicity. Hᵏ := μHE[k]; Lᵏ is Lebesgue measure; ω_k := Lᵏ(B_1). For a measure μ, Θ^k_*(μ, x) := liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(x))/(ω_k r^k) (open balls). M(X) := X.mass for currents in ℝ^P; |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors, and for k-vectors the dual norm. For currents X, Y in the same space, X + Y := X − (0 − Y).
Siblings used. (MR) mass_equals_rep_measure: for IM X with IMRep R in open U, M_G(X) = R.measure(G) for open G; in particular a nonzero IM 0-current has mass ≥ 1. (REP) mass_representation: a current X with locally finite mass in open U has (μ_X, ξ_X) with μ_X(G) = M_G(X) for open G, μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α|, X(ω) = ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X; and if also ∂X has locally finite mass, μ_X(E) = 0 whenever Hᵏ(E) = 0. Consequences: |ξ_X| = 1 μ_X-a.e. (for open G, μ_X(G) = M_G(X) ≤ ∫_G |ξ_X| dμ_X); for a Borel B, X⌞B(ω) := ∫_B ξ_X(ω) dμ_X is a current (linear; sequentially continuous because |X⌞B(ω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ μ_X(tsupport ω)), and for IM X with IMRep (M, θ, ξ) this is the IM restriction: by (MR) and REP, μ_X(G) = M_G(X) = (θHᵏ⌞M)(G) for open G, so the two locally finite Borel measures agree on Borel sets; both (μ_X, ξ_X) and (θHᵏ⌞M, ξ) represent X, so ∫⟨ω, ξ_X − ξ⟩ dμ_X = 0 for all test forms ω, whence ξ_X = ξ μ_X-a.e. (coordinatewise, a finite signed Radon measure on an open set annihilating C_c^∞ is zero). (IMC) im_calculus: locality of approximate tangent spaces (a), IM restrictions (b), differences and integer combinations (c), and (d) for every IMRep the orientation satisfies |orient x α| ≤ |α| for a.e. x of the carrier, so that (R.measure, R.orient) is an admissible representation for (SL) and the integrals below are absolutely convergent. (SL) slicing: for X with representations of X and ∂X and an L-Lipschitz f, the currents X⌞{f < t}, (∂X)⌞{f < t}, Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} with Z_t(η) = 0 if tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅, and M_G(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_X(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}). (DT) deformation_theorem. (VO) vanish_off_support.
Measurable majorant (MM). In the situation of (SL) with G open and F(t) := μ_X(G ∩ {a < f < t}) (nondecreasing, finite if μ_X(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞), M_G(Z_t) ≤ L F'(t) at every t ∈ (a, b) where F is differentiable (a.e., Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt), F' is measurable (Mathlib measurable_deriv) and integrable on [a, b] (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv), and ∫_a^b F' ≤ μ_X(G ∩ {a < f < b}) (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc). For a sequence X_j with sup_j μ_{X_j}(G ∩ {a < f < b}) ≤ Λ, Fatou gives ∫_a^b liminf_j F_j' ≤ Λ, so for a.e. t: every F_j is differentiable at t and liminf_j M_G(Z_{j,t}) ≤ L liminf_j F_j'(t) < ∞.

Part I. Tools.
T1 (Compactness of Radon measures.) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open and μ_j are Borel measures with sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, then a subsequence converges to a Borel measure μ on U, finite on compact subsets of U, in the sense ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ for f ∈ C_c(U); then limsup_j μ_j(C) ≤ μ(C) for compact C ⊆ U and μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for open G ⊆ U. Proof: take compact K_k ↑ U with K_k ⊆ int K_{k+1}; by SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_4_16_compact_metrizable applied to μ_j⌞K_k on the compact metrizable space K_k and a diagonal argument, Λ(f) := lim ∫ f dμ_j exists for every f ∈ C_c(U); Λ is a positive linear functional, so Riesz–Markov–Kakutani (Mathlib RealRMK.rieszMeasure) gives μ. The two inequalities follow by approximating 1_C from above and 1_G from below by functions in C_c(U) (Urysohn).
T2 (Restrictions converge.) Let X_j ⇀ X in 𝒟_k(U) (U open), all with locally finite mass (representations from REP), μ_{X_j} → μ as in T1, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous with μ({f = t}) = 0. Then X_j⌞{f < t} ⇀ X⌞{f < t}. Proof: let ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U) with compact support C ⊆ U and ε > 0. The compact sets C ∩ {f ≤ t − ε} and C ∩ {f ≥ t} are disjoint; choose χ_ε ∈ C_c^∞(U; [0, 1]) equal to 1 on the first and 0 on the second. Then 1_{f<t} − χ_ε vanishes on C outside {t − ε < f < t} and has absolute value ≤ 1, so |X_j⌞{f<t}(ω) − X_j(χ_εω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ μ_{X_j}(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}), whose limsup is ≤ |ω|_∞ μ(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}) (T1, compact set), and this tends to |ω|_∞ μ(C ∩ {f = t}) = 0 as ε ↓ 0. Likewise |X⌞{f<t}(ω) − X(χ_εω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ μ_X(C ∩ {t − ε < f < t}) → 0. Finally X_j(χ_εω) → X(χ_εω).
T3 (Cone inequality.) If X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), k ≥ 1, has finite mass, ∂X = 0 and spt X ⊆ B̄_r(x₀), then |X(ω)| ≤ r M(X)|dω|_∞ for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(ℝ^P). Proof: let (Kγ)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^{j−1} ι_{x−x₀}γ(x₀ + t(x − x₀)) dt for a smooth j-form γ (the homotopy operator of the contraction h_t(x) = x₀ + t(x − x₀)); differentiation under the integral and Cartan's formula d ι_v + ι_v d = L_v for the radial field v(x) = x − x₀ give dKγ + Kdγ = γ − h₀^#γ = γ for j ≥ 1 (h₀ is constant), and |Kγ(x)| ≤ |x − x₀| |γ|_∞/j (|ι_vγ| ≤ |v||γ|). With ζ ∈ C_c^∞ equal to 1 near spt X: X(ω) = X(ζω) = X(ζ dKω) + X(ζ Kdω), and X(ζ dKω) = X(d(ζKω)) − X(dζ ∧ Kω) = ∂X(ζKω) − 0 = 0 by (VO). Hence |X(ω)| ≤ ∫|Kdω| dμ_X ≤ r|dω|_∞ M(X) (μ_X is carried by spt X, REP and VO).
T4 (IM is local.) Let U be open and X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with locally finite mass. If every point of U has an open ball B ⊆ U and an IM current X_B ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with X(ω) = X_B(ω) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ B, then X is IM. Proof: let (μ_X, ξ_X) be the REP representation and (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B) an IMRep of X_B. For open G ⊆ B, the admissible forms for M_G(X) and M_G(X_B) coincide and give the same values, so by REP and (MR) μ_X(G) = M_G(X) = M_G(X_B) = (θ_BHᵏ⌞M_B)(G); two locally finite Borel measures agreeing on the open subsets of B agree on its Borel subsets, so μ_X⌞B = θ_BHᵏ⌞(M_B ∩ B). Both (μ_X, ξ_X) and (μ_X⌞B, ξ_B) represent X on forms supported in B, so ∫⟨ω, ξ_X − ξ_B⟩ dμ_X = 0 for every test form ω supported in B; coordinatewise (a finite signed Radon measure on an open set annihilating C_c^∞ is zero: approximate indicators of compact sets by smooth functions and use dominated convergence and inner regularity) ξ_X = ξ_B μ_X-a.e. on B. Cover U by countably many such balls B_i, put A_i := B_i ∖ ⋃_{l<i} B_l and M := ⋃_i (M_{B_i} ∩ A_i), θ := θ_{B_i}, ξ := ξ_{B_i} on M_{B_i} ∩ A_i. Then X(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵏ; the IMRep fields hold (countable unions of rectifiable sets are rectifiable; θ ≥ 1 integer-valued; ∫_{M∩K}θ dHᵏ = μ_X(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; by IMC(a), for a.e. x ∈ M ∩ A_i the approximate tangent spaces of M, of M ∩ A_i = M_{B_i} ∩ A_i and of M_{B_i} coincide, and ξ_{B_i}(x) orients them).
T5 (Dilations.) For a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let η(y) := λ⁻¹(y − a) and η_#X := the push-forward by this proper affine map (SimonGMT affinePushforward): η_#X(ω) = X(η^#ω), (η^#ω)(y) = λ^{−k}ω(η(y)) (as k-covectors). Then ∂η_# = η_#∂, M_{η(W)}(η_#X) = λ^{−k}M_W(X), spt η_#X = η(spt X); if X = τ(M, θ, ξ) is IM then η_#X = τ(η(M), θ ∘ η⁻¹, ξ ∘ η⁻¹) is IM (Hᵏ(η(A)) = λ^{−k}Hᵏ(A), and the approximate tangent space of η(M) at η(x) is that of M at x because blow-ups commute: η_{η(x),r}(η(M)) = η_{x,λr}(M)); restrictions commute: η_#(X⌞{f ∘ η < t}) = (η_#X)⌞{f < t} (by the change of variables η_#X(ω) = ∫⟨λ^{−k}ω(η(x)), ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X(x), the pair (λ^{−k}η_*μ_X, ξ_X ∘ η⁻¹) represents η_#X, and restrictions do not depend on the representation by (o) of V4).

Part II. Structure of the induction. For d ∈ ℕ let CL(d) be the first conjunct of the statement for currents of degree d (all P, U, T_j, T) and BR(d) the second conjunct for R of degree d + 1. We prove CL(0) (Part III) and, for every d ≥ 0, BR(d) from CL(d) (Part IV) and CL(d+1) from CL(d), BR(d) (Part V). By induction, CL(d) and BR(d) hold for all d, which is the statement.

Part III. CL(0). Let T_j ∈ 𝒟_0(U) be IM with sup_j M_W(T_j) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U (the boundary term is 0 in degree 0) and T_j ⇀ T. In degree 0, H⁰ is counting measure and an IMRep is a set M_j with θ_j ≥ 1 and orientations ±1 (the approximate tangent space at each point of a locally finite set is {0}); local integrability makes M_j ∩ K finite for compact K ⊆ U, so T_j(a) = Σ_{x∈M_j} m_j(x) a(x) with m_j(x) ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} (a ∈ C_c^∞(U) a 0-form). T has locally finite mass (lower semicontinuity). Fix x₀ ∈ U and r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(x₀) ⊆ U, and c := sup_j M_{B_{2r}(x₀)}(T_j) < ∞; by (MR), Σ_{x∈M_j∩B_{2r}(x₀)}|m_j(x)| ≤ c, so on B_{2r}(x₀), T_j = Σ_{i=1}^{N_j} ε_{j,i}δ_{x_{j,i}} with N_j ≤ c, ε_{j,i} = ±1, x_{j,i} ∈ B_{2r}(x₀) (points repeated by multiplicity). Pass to a subsequence with N_j = N, ε_{j,i} = ε_i and x_{j,i} → y_i ∈ B̄_{2r}(x₀). For a ∈ C_c^∞(B_r(x₀)), T(a) = lim_j Σ_i ε_i a(x_{j,i}) = Σ_i ε_i a(y_i). So on B_r(x₀), T agrees with the IM current Σ_{y} m(y)δ_y, m(y) := Σ_{y_i = y}ε_i (points with m(y) = 0 omitted; finite carrier in U). By T4, T is IM.

Part IV. BR(d) from CL(d). Let R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) be IM with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U. If d + 1 > P every (d+1)-current is 0, so R = 0 and ∂R = 0, which is IM: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents the zero current (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero; the positivity, integrability, measurability and orientation fields hold vacuously because μHE restricted to ∅ is the zero measure; and the representing integral over ∅ is 0). Assume d + 1 ≤ P.
1. (Localization.) Fix x₀ ∈ U and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{2r₀}(x₀) ⊆ U; f := |· − x₀|. Apply (SL) to R (IM representation) and ∂R (REP representation); by (MM), for a.e. r ∈ (0, r₀) the slice Z_r := ∂(R⌞B_r(x₀)) − (∂R)⌞B_r(x₀) has finite mass. Fix such r. (The total mass of Z_r is controlled by its mass in G := B_{r₀}(x₀): Z_r vanishes on forms supported off ∂B_r(x₀) ⊆ G, so splitting an admissible form ω = χω + (1 − χ)ω with χ ∈ C_c^∞(G; [0,1]) equal to 1 near ∂B_r(x₀) gives Z_r(ω) = Z_r(χω) ≤ M_G(Z_r).) R' := R⌞B_r(x₀) is IM (IMC(b)) with carrier contained in B_r(x₀), supported in B̄_r(x₀), M(R') < ∞ (MR), and ∂R' = (∂R)⌞B_r(x₀) + Z_r has finite mass. Extend R' to ℝ^P: R̂'(ω) := R'(ζω) with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U) equal to 1 near B̄_r(x₀) (independent of ζ by VO); R̂' is IM with the same IMRep, M(R̂') = M(R'), ∂R̂' = (∂R')^ (VO).
2. (Approximation by the deformation theorem; Simon 6.2.) By (DT) with m := d, K := B̄_r(x₀), Λ := M(R̂'), and ρ_k := 2^{−k}: R̂' − Q_k − S_k = ∂R_k with Q_k and ∂Q_k IM, M(R_k) ≤ cρ_kM(R̂') → 0, M(S_k) ≤ cρ_kM(∂R̂') → 0, M(∂Q_k) ≤ cM(∂R̂'), and spt Q_k ⊆ {dist(·, B̄_r(x₀)) < 3√P ρ_k}. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P), |Q_k(ω) − R̂'(ω)| ≤ M(S_k)|ω|_∞ + M(R_k)|dω|_∞ → 0, so Q_k ⇀ R̂' and ∂Q_k ⇀ ∂R̂'. The ∂Q_k are IM d-currents in ℝ^P with ∂∂Q_k = 0 and bounded masses, so by CL(d) (in U := ℝ^P; the boundary term is M(∂∂Q_k) = 0, or 0 in degree 0), ∂R̂' is IM.
3. (Back to ∂R.) If tsupport η ⊆ B_r(x₀), then ∂R̂'(η) = (∂R)⌞B_r(x₀)(η) + Z_r(η) = ∂R(η) + 0 (η vanishes off B_r(x₀); Z_r(η) = 0 by SL since tsupport η misses {f = r}). The restriction of ∂R̂' to test forms in U is IM: by (MR) and (VO) its IMRep measure vanishes off spt ∂R̂' ⊆ B̄_r(x₀) ⊆ U, so the carrier can be intersected with B̄_r(x₀) without changing the current (IMC(b)), and the resulting data form an IMRep in U. By T4 (∂R has locally finite mass by hypothesis), ∂R is IM. ∎

Part V. CL(n) for n = d + 1 ≥ 1, assuming CL(d) and BR(d).
Let T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be IM, Λ_W := sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U, T_j ⇀ T. If n > P all n-currents vanish and T = 0 is IM (empty representation, as in Part IV); assume n ≤ P.
V1 (Boundaries.) Each ∂T_j is IM by BR(d). T and ∂T have locally finite mass (lower semicontinuity), hence representations (REP).
V2 (Localization; Simon 8.3(1).) Fix x₀ ∈ U, r₀ > 0 with B̄_{2r₀}(x₀) ⊆ U. Pass to a subsequence with μ_{T_j} → μ on U (T1). By (SL) with f := |· − x₀| (representations from IMReps of T_j and ∂T_j, with |orient| ≤ 1 a.e. by IMC(d)) and (MM) (with Λ_{B_{r₀}(x₀)}; total masses of the slices are controlled by their masses in B_{r₀}(x₀) as in IV.1), for a.e. r ∈ (0, r₀), liminf_j M(Z_{j,r}) < ∞, where Z_{j,r} := ∂(T_j⌞B_r(x₀)) − (∂T_j)⌞B_r(x₀); also μ(∂B_r(x₀)) = 0 for all but countably many r. Fix such r and pass to a subsequence with sup_j M(Z_{j,r}) < ∞. Then T'_j := T_j⌞B_r(x₀) are IM (IMC(b)), supported in K := B̄_r(x₀), with sup_j (M(T'_j) + M(∂T'_j)) < ∞, and T'_j ⇀ T⌞B_r(x₀) (T2). Extending to ℝ^P as in IV.1 (carriers inside B_r(x₀)), the extensions T̂'_j are IM with M(∂T̂'_j) = M(∂T'_j) < ∞, so ∂T̂'_j is IM by BR(d) applied in ℝ^P; and T̂'_j ⇀ (T⌞B_r(x₀))^. Then the claim (CL*) below shows that (T⌞B_r(x₀))^ is IM; its restriction to U is IM and agrees with T on forms supported in B_r(x₀). By T4, T is IM. It remains to prove:
(CL*) If T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) are IM, ∂T_j are IM, spt T_j ⊆ K (a fixed compact set), sup_j (M(T_j) + M(∂T_j)) < ∞ and T_j ⇀ T, then T is IM.
V3 (Reduction to cycles; Simon 8.2 and White.) In (CL*), ∂T_j are IM (n−1)-cycles supported in K with bounded masses and ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T, so ∂T is IM by CL(d), with spt ∂T ⊆ K, M(∂T) < ∞ and ∂∂T = 0 (if n − 1 ≥ 1). We find an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with compact support and ∂Y = ∂T:
(Iso) If n − 1 = d ≥ 1 and Z ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) is an IM cycle with compact support, then there is IM Y with ∂Y = Z, M(Y) ≤ c_I M(Z)^{(d+1)/d} and spt Y ⊆ {dist(·, spt Z) < 3√P(2c M(Z))^{1/d}}, where c = c(P, d − 1) is the constant of (DT) and c_I := c(2c)^{1/d}. Proof (Simon 6.1): if Z = 0 take Y = 0 (IM by the empty representation, as in Part IV). Otherwise apply (DT) with m := d − 1, ρ := (2cM(Z))^{1/d}, K := spt Z, Λ := M(Z): Z − Q − S = ∂Y with M(S) ≤ cρM(∂Z) = 0, so S = 0; M(Q) ≤ cM(Z) = ρ^d/2 < ρ^d, so Q = 0 by the dichotomy Q = 0 ∨ M(Q) ≥ ρ^d; hence Z = ∂Y with Y IM, M(Y) ≤ cρM(Z) = c_IM(Z)^{(d+1)/d} and the support bound of (DT).
If n = 1: ∂T is an IM 0-current with compact support, so ∂T = Σ_{i=1}^N m_iδ_{x_i}; with ζ ∈ C_c^∞ equal to 1 near K, ∂T(ζ) = lim_j T_j(dζ) = 0 (VO), i.e. Σm_i = 0; let Y := Σ_i m_i[[x₀, x_i]] (oriented segments from a fixed point x₀ ∉ {x_1, …, x_N}; each is IM — carrier the open segment, multiplicity 1, unit tangent orientation, approximate tangent line at every interior point — and integer combinations are IM by IMC(c)); then ∂Y = Σ m_i(δ_{x_i} − δ_{x₀}) = ∂T.
Put Γ := T − Y. Then Γ is a cycle (∂Γ = ∂T − ∂Y = 0) with compact support (⊆ K ∪ spt Y) and finite mass, and it suffices to show that Γ is IM, because then T = Γ − (0 − Y) is IM (IMC(c)). (Note that the currents T_j − Y are not cycles; the argument below only uses properties of the limit.)
V4 (IM slice property.) For a current X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that X and ∂X have locally finite mass (if n = 1, ∂X is a 0-current and terms involving ∂∂X are absent), with REP representations of X and ∂X, a Lipschitz f and t ∈ ℝ, let ⟨X, f, t⟩ := ∂(X⌞{f < t}) − (∂X)⌞{f < t} (the current Z_t of SL). Say that X has (ISP) if for every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ and L¹-a.e. t, ⟨X, f, t⟩ is IM. For a cycle, ⟨X, f, t⟩ = ∂(X⌞{f < t}).
(o) Linearity. For such X, X' and Borel B, (X − X')⌞B = X⌞B − X'⌞B: the finite-dimensional-vector-valued Radon measures ξ_{X−X'}μ_{X−X'} and ξ_Xμ_X − ξ_{X'}μ_{X'} integrate every smooth compactly supported covector field in the same way, hence (coordinatewise, a finite signed Radon measure on an open set annihilating C_c^∞ is zero: approximate indicators of compact sets by smooth functions and use dominated convergence and inner regularity) agree on bounded Borel sets. Consequently ⟨X − X', f, t⟩ = ⟨X, f, t⟩ − ⟨X', f, t⟩.
(i) If X is IM, ∂X is IM and both have locally finite mass, then X has (ISP): by (SL) and (MM), for a.e. t the slice ⟨X, f, t⟩ has locally finite mass; X⌞{f < t} is IM (IMC(b)) and its boundary (∂X)⌞{f<t} + ⟨X, f, t⟩ has locally finite mass, so it is IM by BR(d); and ⟨X, f, t⟩ = ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} is IM (IMC(b),(c)).
(ii) (ISP) passes to weak limits: let X_i have (ISP), sup_i (μ_{X_i}(B_k(0)) + μ_{∂X_i}(B_k(0))) < ∞ for every k, and X_i ⇀ X. Applying (MM) to the sum of the majorants for X_i (slices ⟨X_i, f, t⟩) and, if n ≥ 2, for ∂X_i (slices ⟨∂X_i, f, t⟩ = ∂((∂X_i)⌞{f<t}), as ∂∂X_i = 0), on each interval (−m, m) (and then for all m simultaneously, countably many conditions) we get for a.e. t: μ({f = t}) = μ'({f = t}) = 0; liminf_i (M_{B_{k+1}(0)}(⟨X_i, f, t⟩) + M_{B_{k+1}(0)}(⟨∂X_i, f, t⟩)) < ∞; and ⟨X_i, f, t⟩ is IM for every i. Fix such t and a further subsequence along which these masses are bounded. By T2 applied to X_i and to ∂X_i, ⟨X_i, f, t⟩ ⇀ ⟨X, f, t⟩; and ∂⟨X_i, f, t⟩ = −∂((∂X_i)⌞{f<t}) = −⟨∂X_i, f, t⟩ has bounded mass in B_{k+1}(0) (for n = 1 the slices are 0-currents and there is no boundary term). The domain restrictions to U' := B_{k+1}(0) of the IM currents ⟨X_i, f, t⟩ are IM (intersect their carriers with U', IMC(b) in ℝ^P), with bounded mass and boundary mass in U', and converge weakly in U'; by CL(d) in U', the domain restriction of ⟨X, f, t⟩ to U' is IM. Intersecting its carrier with B_k(0) (IMC(b) in U') and extending by A ↦ (ω ↦ A(ζω)), ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U') equal to 1 near B̄_k(0) (as in IV.1; an IMRep with carrier in B_k(0) is an IMRep in ℝ^P), gives an IM current in ℝ^P agreeing with ⟨X, f, t⟩ on forms supported in B_k(0). ⟨X, f, t⟩ has locally finite mass (lower semicontinuity of mass under the above weak convergence). For a.e. t this holds for all k, and T4 shows that ⟨X, f, t⟩ is IM. So X has (ISP).
(iii) (ISP) is invariant under the dilations of T5 (slices of η_#X by f are η_# of slices of X by f ∘ η, and η_# preserves IM).
Application: the T_j have (ISP) by (i) (T_j, ∂T_j IM, bounded masses); by (ii), T has (ISP); Y has (ISP) by (i) (Y IM with compact support, ∂Y = ∂T IM, finite masses); by (o) and IMC(c), Γ = T − Y has (ISP), i.e. ∂(Γ⌞{f < t}) is IM for every Lipschitz f and a.e. t.

Iterating with A ∖ ⋃F_k(ℝⁿ) (Borel, as the F_k(ℝⁿ) are σ-compact) shows that M' is covered by countably many Lipschitz images up to an Hⁿ-null set, i.e. M' is countably n-rectifiable.
Proof of the claim (Simon, with the corrected ε). For x with P_x: with π_x := P_x^⊥ and X_α(π, x) := {y : dist(y − x, π) < α|y − x|}, the definition of P_x (testing with continuous functions approximating 1_{B_1} and 1_{X̄_{1/2}(π_x,0) ∩ B̄_1}, whose boundaries are Hⁿ⌞P_x-null, and X̄_{1/2}(π_x, 0) ∩ P_x = {0}) gives (5) μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 1 and (6) μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 0. By Lusin's theorem (SimonGMT Chapter01 exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable, applied to the finitely many coordinates of the projection matrix of P_x, a Borel function of x by V12, and intersecting the closed sets obtained; μ finite) take a closed F ⊆ A with μ(ℝ^P ∖ F) ≤ μ(ℝ^P)/4 on which x ↦ P_x is continuous and (5), (6) hold; the functions f_k(x) := inf_{ρ<1/k} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) and q_k(x) := sup_{ρ<1/k} μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) are Borel on F (countable inf/sup over rational ρ of semicontinuous functions, by left continuity in ρ and continuity of x ↦ π_x on F), f_k → 1 and q_k → 0 on F; by Egorov (Mathlib MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto) choose a closed E ⊆ F with μ(F ∖ E) ≤ μ(ℝ^P)/4 and uniform convergence on E. With ε := 2^{−1}16^{−n} there is δ > 0 such that μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ (1 − ε)ω_nρⁿ and μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ εω_nρⁿ for x ∈ E, ρ < δ. Choose ℓ-dimensional subspaces π_1, …, π_N (ℓ := P − n) such that every ℓ-subspace π has ‖p_π − p_{π_j}‖ < 1/16 for some j, and E_j := {x ∈ E : ‖p_{π_j} − p_{π_x}‖ < 1/16}. Then (10): X_{1/4}(π_j, x) ∩ E_j ∩ B_{δ/2}(x) = ∅ for x ∈ E_j (x itself never lies in X_{1/4}(π_j, x), the defining inequality being strict). Otherwise there is y ∈ X_{1/4}(π_j, x) ∩ E_j with σ := |y − x| ∈ (0, δ/2); for z ∈ B_{σ/8}(y), dist(z − x, π_x) ≤ dist(y − x, π_j) + σ/16 + σ/8 < 7σ/16 ≤ |z − x|/2, so B_{σ/8}(y) ⊆ X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_{2σ}(x), whence (1 − ε)ω_n(σ/8)ⁿ ≤ μ(B_{σ/8}(y)) ≤ εω_n(2σ)ⁿ, i.e. (1 − ε)8^{−n} ≤ ε2ⁿ = 8^{−n}/2, a contradiction. By (10), for any x₀ ∈ ℝ^P the orthogonal projection p_j onto π_j^⊥ ≅ ℝⁿ satisfies |p_j(y) − p_j(x)| ≥ |y − x|/4 for x, y ∈ E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀) (then |x − y| < δ/2); so E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀) is the graph over p_j(E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀)) of a Lipschitz map into π_j, which extends to a Lipschitz map on π_j^⊥ (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi componentwise in an orthonormal basis of π_j; the constant changes by a factor √ℓ), i.e. E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀) ⊆ F(ℝⁿ) for a Lipschitz F. E is compact (closed and bounded), so finitely many balls B_{δ/4}(x₀) cover E, and the finitely many pieces E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀) cover E, and μ(ℝ^P ∖ ⋃F_k(ℝⁿ)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P ∖ E) ≤ μ(ℝ^P)/2. ∎
V14 (Integrality; replaces Simon (7)–(10).) At a as in V12, C = τ₀Hⁿ⌞V₀ = θ₀[[V₀]] with [[V₀]] oriented by v_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ v_n, and C has (ISP) (V8). For f(y) := ⟨y, v_1⟩ (1-Lipschitz) and every t, the divergence theorem in V₀ ≅ ℝⁿ on the half-space {f < t} gives ∂(C⌞{f < t}) = θ₀[[V₀ ∩ {f = t}]] with orientation ±v_2 ∧ ⋯ ∧ v_n (for n = 1: ±θ₀δ_{tv_1}). For a.e. t this current is IM; by (MR) its mass measure is θ₀H^{n−1}⌞(V₀ ∩ {f = t}) and also θ'H^{n−1}⌞M_t for an IMRep (M_t, θ', ·) with θ' ≥ 1 integer; uniqueness of Radon–Nikodym densities on the plane gives θ₀ = θ' a.e. on a set of positive measure, so θ₀ ∈ ℤ (for n = 1, θ₀ = θ'(tv_1)). Hence θ(a) is a positive integer for Hⁿ-a.e. a ∈ M'.
V15 (Conclusion of CL*.) Let M'' ⊆ M' be a Borel set with Hⁿ(M' ∖ M'') = 0 such that at every point of M'' V12 and V14 hold and θ is a positive integer (Borel regularity; the sets where these fail are null); put mult := the ℕ-valued Borel function equal to θ on M'' and 0 elsewhere (so mult ≥ 1 at every point of the carrier), orient := ξ_Γ = τ/θ. Then (M'', θ, ξ_Γ) is an IMRep in ℝ^P: M'' Borel and countably n-rectifiable (V13), θ ≥ 1, ∫θ dHⁿ = M(Γ) < ∞, ξ_Γ a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M'' (it is for μ_Γ = θHⁿ⌞M', and θ > 0 on M'' makes the two measures mutually absolutely continuous on M''), and for a.e. a ∈ M'' the approximate tangent space of M'' at a is V₀(a) (V12 and IMC(a)), oriented by ξ_Γ(a). It represents Γ by V6. So Γ is IM, hence T = Γ − (0 − Y) is IM (IMC(c)), which proves (CL*) and hence, by V2, CL(n). ∎

This completes the induction (Parts II–V), proving both conjuncts.
proof_key_steps: Joint induction: CL(0) directly (finite point masses); BR(d) from CL(d) via approximation by the deformation theorem and localization by slicing; CL(d+1) from CL(d) and BR(d).
Localization (Simon 8.3(1)) by slicing and restriction convergence; IM is a local property; reduction to compact supports in ℝ^P.
Reduction to the cycle Γ = T − Y, with ∂Y = ∂T filled by the isoperimetric inequality (from the deformation theorem) or by segments; the IM slice property passes to weak limits, so Γ has it.
Simon 8.2 lower density bound Θⁿ_* ≥ η₀ via isoperimetric fillings, the cone inequality and Besicovitch covering.

White-type blow-up at Lebesgue points: limits are τ₀ν with ν invariant along an n-plane V₀, τ₀ simple, ν a finite sum of parallel planes, each of multiplicity ≥ 1 by a projection/mollification argument; so the tangent measure is Hⁿ⌞V₀.
Approximate tangent planes a.e. give rectifiability (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 ⇐, corrected constant); slices give integer multiplicity; assemble the IMRep.

audit.reason: The joint induction is well-founded: CL(0), BR(d) from CL(d), then CL(d+1) from CL(d) and BR(d). Localization, slice stability, lower density, the constant-vector blow-up and projection argument, rectifiability and integer densities establish both exact conjuncts without using flat convergence or the parent theorem.

subproblem.title: Weak convergence implies local flat convergence for integer multiplicity currents (Simon Ch. 6, 7.2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every open W with closure(W) compact and contained in U, and T_j ⇀ T in U. Then for every such open W there are integer multiplicity R_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with T − T_j − S_j = ∂R_j for every j (Simon writes this as T − T_j = ∂R_j + S_j) and M_W(R_j) + M_W(S_j) → 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + (Ts j).boundary.massOn W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ∃ (R : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 2)) (S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (R j) ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity (S j) ∧ T - Ts j - S j = (R j).boundary) ∧ Tendsto (fun j => (R j).massOn W + (S j).massOn W) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 7.2, “only if” direction, with Definition 7.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 2004–2140, printed pp. 170–172). Simon's proof uses the deformation theorem 5.3 (here the sibling deformation_theorem), the slicing estimates 4.5(1),(2) for the localization (here the sibling slicing), the completeness Lemma 3.13 (here replaced by the sibling closure theorem, see step 6) and, tacitly, the boundary rectifiability theorem 6.3 to make the deformation remainders S integer multiplicity (here the sibling closure_and_boundary_rectifiability, part (BR)). Notation: n := m + 1; IM := integer multiplicity; for currents X, Y in the same space, X + Y := X − (0 − Y) (contract Sub); M(X) := M_{ℝ^P}(X) = X.mass for currents in ℝ^P; M_G(X) := X.massOn G.

Sibling facts used.
(S1) [mass_equals_rep_measure] For IM X in an open set with representation R, M_G(X) = R.measure(G) for open G; in particular M_W(X) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U and, for Borel B, the IM restriction X⌞B (sibling im_calculus (b), carrier ∩ B) has M_G(X⌞B) = R.measure(G ∩ B).
(S2) [im_calculus] IM currents in an open set are closed under − (conjunct (c)), hence under + (X + Y := X − (0 − Y), with 0 = X − X IM by (c)) and finite integer combinations, and restrictions of IMReps to Borel sets represent IM currents (conjunct (b)). In addition (direct check, used in the degenerate cases of step 0 and in step 1) the zero current in any degree is IM: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents the zero current (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero; the positivity, integrability, measurability and orientation fields hold vacuously because μHE restricted to ∅ is the zero measure; and the representing integral over ∅ is 0).
(S3) [closure_and_boundary_rectifiability] (CL) weak limits of IM currents with locally bounded M + M∂ are IM; (BR) the boundary of an IM current with locally finite boundary mass is IM.
(S4) [slicing] For a current with representations of itself and its boundary and a 1-Lipschitz f: the restricted currents A_t, B_t, the support property, and M_G(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}).
(S5) [vanish_off_support] X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt X = ∅.
(S6) [deformation_theorem] For P, m there is c ≥ 1 such that for ρ > 0, compact K and Λ ≥ 0 there is a finite set 𝒬 of currents in ℝ^P with: every IM T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with spt T ⊆ K, M(T) ≤ Λ, M(∂T) < ∞ satisfies T − Q − S = ∂R with Q ∈ 𝒬, Q and R IM, M(R) ≤ cρM(T), M(S) ≤ cρM(∂T), spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ thickening(3√P ρ, spt T).
For an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) the orientation satisfies |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| Hⁿ-a.e. on M (sibling im_calculus, conjunct (d)), so (R.measure, ξ) is a representation in the sense of (S4).

Proof.
0. (Trivial cases.) If n > P every n- and (n+1)-current vanishes; take R_j := 0, S_j := 0 (then T − T_j − S_j = 0 = ∂R_j and the masses are 0). If W = ∅ (in particular if U = ∅), take R_j := 0 and S_j := T − T_j (IM by S2): T − T_j − S_j = 0 = ∂0 and every M_∅ vanishes. Assume n ≤ P and W ≠ ∅.
1. (Reduction to the flat distance.) For X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) let d_W(X) := inf{M_W(R) + M_W(S) : R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) both IM, X − S = ∂R}. For X := T − T_j the choice R = 0, S = T − T_j (IM by S2) gives d_W(T − T_j) ≤ M_W(T − T_j) < ∞ (S1, W ⊂⊂ U). If d_W(T − T_j) → 0, choosing for each j an admissible pair with M_W(R_j) + M_W(S_j) ≤ d_W(T − T_j) + 2^{−j} proves the theorem. By the subsequence principle for real sequences it suffices to show: every subsequence of (T_j) has a further subsequence (j_ℓ) with d_W(T − T_{j_ℓ}) → 0. Fix a subsequence and keep calling it T_j; the hypotheses remain true for it.
2. (Boundaries.) Each ∂T_j is IM by (S3)(BR) (T_j IM, M_G(∂T_j) < ∞ for G ⊂⊂ U); ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), so M_G(T) + M_G(∂T) ≤ liminf_j (M_G(T_j) + M_G(∂T_j)) < ∞ for G ⊂⊂ U (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf). T is IM by hypothesis; fix an IMRep R_T of T and put μ_T := R_T.measure, which is finite on compact subsets of U; for Borel B, T⌞B denotes the IM restriction (S2).
3. (Localization; Simon (4).) Let δ₀ > 0 with 3δ₀ < infDist(closure W, ℝ^P ∖ U) (δ₀ := 1 if U = ℝ^P), g(x) := infDist(x, closure W) (1-Lipschitz; closure W ≠ ∅ is compact), W₁ := {g < 5δ₀/2} ⊂⊂ U and Λ₀ := sup_j (M_{W₁}(T_j) + M_{W₁}(∂T_j)) < ∞. Let R_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j), R'_j = (M'_j, θ'_j, ξ'_j) be IMReps of T_j, ∂T_j and μ_j := R_j.measure, μ'_j := R'_j.measure (finite on compact subsets of U). By (S4) with f = g we get currents A_{j,s} = T_j⌞{g < s} (= the IM restriction, S2), B_{j,s} = (∂T_j)⌞{g < s} and Z_{j,s} := ∂A_{j,s} − B_{j,s} with M(Z_{j,s}) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_j({s − h < g < s}) for s ∈ (0, 2δ₀). First, the restrictions of the μ_j to the compact metrizable space K₀ := {g ≤ 2δ₀} ⊆ W₁ have total mass ≤ Λ₀, so by SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_4_16_compact_metrizable a subsequence (still T_j) satisfies μ_j⌞K₀ → ν weakly on K₀ (against C(K₀)) for a finite Borel measure ν on K₀; the level sets {g = s}, 0 < s < 2δ₀, are disjoint, so ν({g = s}) > 0 for at most countably many s (Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos). Next, for this subsequence, the function F_j(s) := μ_j({0 < g < min(s, 2δ₀)}) is nondecreasing on ℝ with F_j ≤ Λ₀; at every point s ∈ (0, 2δ₀) of differentiability (a.e., Lebesgue) the pointwise bound of (S4) gives M(Z_{j,s}) ≤ F_j'(s) (μ_j({s − h < g < s}) ≤ F_j(s) − F_j(s − h)), F_j' = deriv F_j is measurable (Mathlib measurable_deriv), F_j' is integrable on [0, 2δ₀] (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv), and ∫_0^{2δ₀} F_j' ≤ Λ₀ (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc). Fatou's lemma gives ∫_0^{2δ₀} liminf_j F_j'(s) ds ≤ Λ₀, so liminf_j F_j'(s) < ∞ for a.e. s. Fix s ∈ (δ₀, 2δ₀) with liminf_j F_j'(s) < ∞, F_j differentiable at s for all j, and ν({g = s}) = 0; pass to a further subsequence with sup_j M(Z_{j,s}) =: Λ₁ < ∞ (weak convergence on K₀ is inherited by subsequences). Put T'_j := A_{j,s}, G := {g < s} (open, W ⊆ G, closure G ⊆ {g ≤ s} =: K, a compact subset of W₁ ⊆ U).
 (a) T'_j is IM (S2) with spt T'_j ⊆ K (T'_j(ω) = 0 whenever ω vanishes on G, in particular whenever tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅), M(T'_j) ≤ μ_j(G) ≤ Λ₀, ∂T'_j = B_{j,s} + Z_{j,s} so M(∂T'_j) ≤ μ'_j(G) + Λ₁ ≤ Λ₀ + Λ₁ =: Λ, and ∂T'_j is IM by (S3)(BR).
 (b) T'_j ⇀ T' := T⌞G: for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and ε > 0 let χ_ε ∈ C_c^∞(G; [0, 1]) with χ_ε = 1 on G_ε := {g < s − ε}. Then |T'_j(ω) − T_j(χ_εω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ μ_j({s − ε ≤ g < s}) and limsup_j μ_j({s − ε ≤ g ≤ s}) ≤ ν({s − ε ≤ g ≤ s}) (weak convergence on K₀, closed set), which tends to ν({g = s}) = 0 as ε ↓ 0; also |T'(ω) − T(χ_εω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ μ_T({s − ε ≤ g < s}) → 0; and T_j(χ_εω) → T(χ_εω). Hence T'_j(ω) → T'(ω).
 (c) (Extension to ℝ^P.) For a current X in U whose support lies in K, X̂(ω) := X(ζω) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)), with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U; [0, 1]) equal to 1 near K (a test form in U is in particular a test form on ℝ^P, and ζω is a test form in U), defines a current in ℝ^P independent of ζ (S5), with the same masses on open sets, ∂X̂ = (∂X)^ (because X(dζ ∧ ·) = 0 by S5), and if X is IM with a carrier contained in K then X̂ is IM with the same IMRep. All of this applies to T'_j and T', and T̂'_j ⇀ T̂'. Conversely, restricting the domain of a current in ℝ^P to 𝒟(U) (contract restrictDomain) preserves IM-ness when a carrier lies in U and does not increase masses.
4. (Deformation; Simon (2), (3).) Let c be the constant of (S6) for (P, m). Given η > 0 choose ρ ∈ (0, δ₀/(4√P)) with 2cρΛ < η (so 3√Pρ < 3δ₀/4) and apply (S6) with (ρ, K, Λ): there is a finite 𝒬 and for every j a decomposition T̂'_j − Q_j − S'_j = ∂R'_j with Q_j ∈ 𝒬 and Q_j, R'_j IM, M(R'_j) ≤ cρΛ, M(S'_j) ≤ cρΛ, and spt Q_j ∪ spt R'_j ⊆ K' := {g ≤ s + 3δ₀/4} (compact, contained in {g ≤ 11δ₀/4} ⊆ U because 3δ₀ < infDist(closure W, ℝ^P ∖ U)). S'_j is IM: ∂R'_j has finite mass (≤ M(T̂'_j) + M(Q_j) + M(S'_j)), so it is IM by (S3)(BR) applied in ℝ^P, and S'_j = T̂'_j − Q_j − ∂R'_j is IM by (S2). spt S'_j ⊆ K' as well (S'_j = T̂'_j − Q_j − ∂R'_j and spt ∂R'_j ⊆ spt R'_j). Since 𝒬 is finite, some Q ∈ 𝒬 equals Q_j for infinitely many j; for any two such j, l: T̂'_j − T̂'_l − (S'_j − S'_l) = ∂(R'_j − R'_l), with R'_j − R'_l and S'_j − S'_l IM (S2), supported in K', and M(R'_j − R'_l) + M(S'_j − S'_l) ≤ 4cρΛ < 2η.
5. (Cauchy subsequence; Simon (5).) Applying step 4 successively with η = 2^{−r−1}, r = 1, 2, …, to nested infinite index sets, we obtain j_1 < j_2 < ⋯ and IM R_r ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P), S_r ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) supported in K' with T̂'_{j_{r+1}} − T̂'_{j_r} − S_r = ∂R_r and M(R_r) + M(S_r) ≤ 2^{−r}.
6. (Summation; Simon's use of 3.13.) For ℓ < N let R^{(ℓ,N)} := Σ_{ℓ≤r<N} R_r and S^{(ℓ,N)} := Σ_{ℓ≤r<N} S_r (IM by S2). Summing step 5, T̂'_{j_N} − T̂'_{j_ℓ} − S^{(ℓ,N)} = ∂R^{(ℓ,N)}. Define R^{(ℓ)}(ω) := Σ_{r≥ℓ} R_r(ω) and S^{(ℓ)}(ω) := Σ_{r≥ℓ} S_r(ω); the series converge absolutely since |R_r(ω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ M(R_r) (definition of mass: ±ω/|ω|_∞ is admissible for M_{ℝ^P}), they define currents (uniform bound |R^{(ℓ)}(ω)| ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}|ω|_∞ gives sequential continuity), M(R^{(ℓ)}) + M(S^{(ℓ)}) ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}, and R^{(ℓ,N)} ⇀ R^{(ℓ)}, S^{(ℓ,N)} ⇀ S^{(ℓ)} as N → ∞. These limits are IM by (S3)(CL) applied in ℝ^P: M(R^{(ℓ,N)}) ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}, M(∂R^{(ℓ,N)}) = M(T̂'_{j_N} − T̂'_{j_ℓ} − S^{(ℓ,N)}) ≤ 2Λ₀ + 1, M(S^{(ℓ,N)}) ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}, and ∂S^{(ℓ,N)} = ∂T̂'_{j_N} − ∂T̂'_{j_ℓ} (apply ∂ to the identity, ∂∂ = 0) has mass ≤ 2Λ. Letting N → ∞ (T̂'_{j_N} ⇀ T̂' and ∂ is weakly continuous) gives T̂' − T̂'_{j_ℓ} − S^{(ℓ)} = ∂R^{(ℓ)}, with spt R^{(ℓ)}, spt S^{(ℓ)} ⊆ K' ⊆ U.
7. (Back to U.) Restrict the domains of R^{(ℓ)}, S^{(ℓ)} to U (contract restrictDomain). These are IM in U: take IMReps in ℝ^P; by (S1) and (S5) their measures vanish outside the support, which lies in K' ⊆ U, so intersecting the carriers with U (S2(b) applied in ℝ^P with E = U) does not change the currents, and the resulting data form IMReps in U representing the domain restrictions. In U, T = T⌞G + T⌞(ℝ^P ∖ G) and T_{j_ℓ} = T_{j_ℓ}⌞G + T_{j_ℓ}⌞(ℝ^P ∖ G) (additivity of the representing integrals), and T⌞G, T_{j_ℓ}⌞G are the domain restrictions of T̂', T̂'_{j_ℓ}. Hence T − T_{j_ℓ} − S♯_ℓ = ∂R^{(ℓ)} in U with
 S♯_ℓ := S^{(ℓ)} + T⌞(ℝ^P ∖ G) − T_{j_ℓ}⌞(ℝ^P ∖ G).
T is IM by hypothesis, so T⌞(ℝ^P ∖ G) is IM (S2), and S♯_ℓ is IM (S2). Every ω admissible for M_W has tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ G, so the last two terms vanish on it; hence M_W(S♯_ℓ) ≤ M(S^{(ℓ)}) and M_W(R^{(ℓ)}) ≤ M(R^{(ℓ)}). Thus d_W(T − T_{j_ℓ}) ≤ 2^{1−ℓ} → 0 along the sub-subsequence, which by step 1 proves the theorem. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to d_W(T − T_j) → 0 and, by the subsequence principle, to a sub-subsequence statement.
Localize to T′_j = T_j⌞{g < s} with bounded M + M∂ and IM boundaries (slicing, measurable majorants, Fatou, Radon compactness on a compact set, restriction convergence); extend to ℝ^P.
Total boundedness from the deformation theorem: all Q_j lie in one finite set 𝒬; remainders S′ are IM by (BR); pigeonhole gives flat-close pairs.
Extract a flat-Cauchy subsequence and sum the series; the limits R^{(ℓ)}, S^{(ℓ)} are IM by the closure theorem (replacing Simon 3.13).
Return to U and absorb T⌞(ℝ^P∖G) − T_{j_ℓ}⌞(ℝ^P∖G) into S, which has no mass in W.

subproblem.title: Local comparison inequality for weak limits of minimizing currents (Simon 7.2.4, (1)–(11))
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and T_j (j ∈ ℕ), T ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Assume: (i) each T_j is minimizing in U (contract IsMinimizingIn T_j U: T_j is integer multiplicity and M_W(T_j) ≤ M_W(S') whenever W is open with closure(W) compact and contained in U, S' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity, ∂S' = ∂T_j, and spt(S' − T_j) is a compact subset of U ∩ W); (ii) sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every open W with closure(W) compact and contained in U; (iii) T_j ⇀ T in U; (iv) T is integer multiplicity. Then for every compact K ⊆ U and every ε > 0 there exist an open set W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) := {x : |x − y| < ε for some y ∈ K} (Mathlib Metric.thickening ε K) and closure(W) compact and contained in U, a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and numbers e_j ∈ [0, ∞] with e_j → 0, such that M_W(T_{φ(j)}) ≤ M_W(S) + e_j for every j ∈ ℕ and every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with ∂S = ∂T and spt(S − T) ⊆ K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsMinimizingIn (Ts j) U) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + (Ts j).boundary.massOn W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → ∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → 0 < ε → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W ∧ K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ CompactlyContained W U ∧ ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞), StrictMono φ ∧ Tendsto e atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ S : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity S → S.boundary = T.boundary → (S - T).support ⊆ K → ∀ j, (Ts (φ j)).massOn W ≤ S.massOn W + e j
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.2.4, proof of (1)–(11) (chapter-07.txt lines 176–258); these are steps 3–7 of the parent proof. Departures from the printed text are marked “Correction”.

Conventions. n = m + 1 ≥ 1; “W ⊂⊂ U” means W open with closure(W) compact and contained in U; M(A) := M_{ℝ^P}(A) = A.mass; IM means integer multiplicity; for currents X, Y in U, X + Y := X − (0 − Y) (contract Sub). For an IM current A ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with an IMRep R_A put μ_A := R_A.measure.

Sibling facts used.
(F1) [mass_equals_rep_measure] M_G(A) = μ_A(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P (U open). Hence μ_A does not depend on the representation on open sets, hence (finite on compact subsets of U, outer regular) on Borel subsets of U; μ_A(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0; M(A) = μ_A(ℝ^P); and for compact E ⊆ U, μ_A(E) = lim_{δ↓0} μ_A(E_δ), E_δ := {x : dist(x, E) < δ}.
(F2) [vanish_off_support] A(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt A = ∅. With (F1): μ_A(ℝ^P ∖ spt A) = μ_A(U ∖ spt A) = 0 (U ∖ spt A is open and every admissible form for M_{U∖spt A}(A) is killed).
(F3) (Simon 2.11, definitional) spt ∂A ⊆ spt A (∂A(ω) = A(dω), tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω); spt(A ± B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B; a support contained in a compact subset of U is compact (supports are relatively closed in U).
(F4) [im_calculus (c)] A − B (hence A + B and integer combinations) is IM if A, B are; and M_G(A ± B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) for open G (definition of M_G), so by (F1) μ_{A±B}(E) ≤ μ_A(E) + μ_B(E) for compact E ⊆ U (apply to E_δ, let δ ↓ 0).
(F5) [im_calculus (b)] For IM A and Borel B, A⌞B, represented by (M_A ∩ B, θ_A, ξ_A), is IM; (A⌞B)(ω) = A(ω) if ω vanishes outside B (in particular if B is open and tsupport ω ⊆ B); μ_{A⌞B} = μ_A⌞B; spt(A⌞B) ⊆ closure(B) ∩ U; M(A⌞B) = μ_A(B).
(F6) [flat_convergence] If T, T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are IM, sup_j (M_G(T_j) + M_G(∂T_j)) < ∞ for G ⊂⊂ U and T_j ⇀ T, then for every G ⊂⊂ U there are IM R_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U), S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with T − T_j − S_j = ∂R_j and M_G(R_j) + M_G(S_j) → 0.
(F7) [slicing] For a current R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) with representations (μ, ξ) of R and (μ', ξ') of ∂R and an L-Lipschitz f: the currents A_t = R⌞{f < t}, B_t = (∂R)⌞{f < t} (integrals over {f < t}), Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t, with Z_t(η) = 0 when tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅, and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_G(Z_t) dt ≤ L μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}) and M_G(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for open G.
(F8) [closure_and_boundary_rectifiability (BR)] The boundary of an IM current in U with locally finite boundary mass is IM.
For an IMRep, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| Hᵈ-a.e. on the carrier (sibling im_calculus, conjunct (d)), so (R.measure, orient) is a representation in the sense of (F7), and for Borel B the current of (F7) built from it coincides with the IM restriction of (F5).

Dimension remark. If n > P, every n-covector on ℝ^P vanishes, so every n-current is 0; then the conclusion holds with W as constructed in steps 1–2 below (W := ∅ if K = ∅, W := W₀ otherwise), φ := id and e_j := 0. Otherwise (F6) applies in every codimension (including n = P, where (n+1)-currents vanish).

Proof.
1. (Trivial case.) If K = ∅, take W := ∅ (open, closure ∅ compact and contained in U, K ⊆ ∅ ⊆ thickening), φ := id and e_j := 0; only the zero form has support in ∅, so M_∅(T_j) = 0. Assume K ≠ ∅.
2. (Cut-off; lines 176–186.) Let d₀ := dist(K, ℝ^P ∖ U) ∈ (0, ∞] (d₀ := ∞ if U = ℝ^P) and δ := min(ε, d₀)/2, so 0 < δ < ε and C := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ δ} is a compact subset of U. Choose ψ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on K and tsupport ψ ⊆ {dist(·, K) < δ} (mollify the indicator of {dist(·, K) < δ/2} at scale δ/4). ψ is Lipschitz with constant L := sup|Dψ| < ∞. For 0 ≤ s < 1 put W_s := {ψ > s}: open, K ⊆ W_s ⊆ {dist(·, K) < δ} ⊆ thickening ε K, closure(W_s) ⊆ tsupport ψ ⊆ C, so W_s ⊂⊂ U. For 0 < s < 1: {ψ ≥ s} is a closed subset of tsupport ψ, hence compact; closure(W_s) ⊆ {ψ ≥ s}; {ψ ≥ s} ⊆ W_γ for 0 ≤ γ < s; ⋂_{0<γ<s} W_γ = {ψ ≥ s}; and {ψ = s} ∩ K = ∅.
3. (Flat convergence; (2), lines 187–191.) By hypothesis every T_j is minimizing, hence IM, T is IM, and the mass bounds and T_j ⇀ T hold; (F6) with G := W₀ gives IM R_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U), S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with T − T_j − S_j = ∂R_j and M_{W₀}(R_j) + M_{W₀}(S_j) → 0.
4. (Slicing; (3)–(4), lines 192–201.) ∂R_j = T − T_j − S_j is IM (F4), so R_j and ∂R_j have IM representations whose measures μ_{R_j}, μ_{∂R_j} are finite on compact subsets of U (F1). Apply (F7) to R_j with f := −ψ (Lipschitz constant L) and t := −s, so that {f < t} = W_s: the currents A_t = R_j⌞W_s and B_t = (∂R_j)⌞W_s are the IM restrictions (F5), and
 P_{j,s} := ∂(R_j⌞W_s) − (∂R_j)⌞W_s
satisfies P_{j,s}(η) = 0 whenever tsupport η ∩ {ψ = s} = ∅, and, since {t − h < f < t} = {s < ψ < s + h},
 M_{W₀}(P_{j,s}) ≤ L liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ_{R_j}(W₀ ∩ {s < ψ < s + h}) for every s ∈ (0, 1).
(a) Localization of the mass of P_{j,s}: for s ∈ (0, 1) the closed set {ψ = s} is a compact subset of W₀. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(W₀; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 near {ψ = s}. For any open G and any ω admissible for M_G, (1 − χ)ω vanishes near {ψ = s}, so P_{j,s}(ω) = P_{j,s}(χω) ≤ M_{W₀}(P_{j,s}) (χω is admissible for M_{W₀}). Hence M_G(P_{j,s}) ≤ M_{W₀}(P_{j,s}) for every open G, in particular M(P_{j,s}) ≤ M_{W₀}(P_{j,s}).
(b) Integrality: if M_{W₀}(P_{j,s}) < ∞, then ∂(R_j⌞W_s) = (∂R_j)⌞W_s + P_{j,s} has locally finite mass (by (a) and μ_{∂R_j}(G) < ∞ for G ⊂⊂ U), R_j⌞W_s is IM (F5), so ∂(R_j⌞W_s) is IM by (F8) and P_{j,s} is IM by (F4), (F5); and spt P_{j,s} ⊆ {ψ = s} (vanishing property). Thus ∂(R_j⌞W_s) = (∂R_j)⌞W_s + P_{j,s}, Simon's (3).
Remark (not an erratum): Simon's spt P_j ⊆ ∂W_α also holds, but only spt P_j ⊆ {ψ = α} (⊇ ∂W_α) is used. The sign convention is that of Simon 4.6 with f = −ψ, which yields exactly (3).
5. (Choice of α and φ; (3)–(5), lines 192–205.) Let H_j(s) := μ_{R_j}(W₀ ∩ {s < ψ < 1}) for every s ∈ ℝ: a nonincreasing real function (finite, bounded by μ_{R_j}(W₀) = M_{W₀}(R_j) < ∞ since closure W₀ is a compact subset of U; F1). For 0 < h < 1 − s, {s < ψ < s + h} ⊆ {s < ψ < 1} ∖ {s + h < ψ < 1}, so μ_{R_j}(W₀ ∩ {s < ψ < s + h}) ≤ H_j(s) − H_j(s + h). By Lebesgue's theorem (Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt applied to −H_j) H_j is differentiable a.e., and at such s step 4 gives M_{W₀}(P_{j,s}) ≤ g_j(s) := −L H_j'(s). The functions g_j ≥ 0 are measurable (Mathlib measurable_deriv) and ∫_0^1 g_j ≤ L(H_j(0) − H_j(1)) ≤ L M_{W₀}(R_j) (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv and MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc applied to the nondecreasing function −H_j). Since M_{W₀}(R_j) → 0 (step 3), Fatou's lemma gives ∫_0^1 liminf_j g_j ≤ liminf_j ∫_0^1 g_j = 0, so liminf_j g_j(s) = 0 for a.e. s. For each j, the level sets {ψ = s} (0 < s < 1) are pairwise disjoint subsets of the compact set tsupport ψ ⊆ U, on which μ_{T_j} is finite (F1), so μ_{T_j}({ψ = s}) > 0 for at most countably many s. Hence there is α ∈ (0, 1) such that: every H_j is differentiable at α (so M_{W₀}(P_{j,α}) ≤ g_j(α) < ∞ and step 4(b) applies at s = α for every j); liminf_j g_j(α) = 0; and μ_{T_j}({ψ = α}) = 0 for every j.
